devdoc.details: THE ARMY REGISTRY, RESOLVED: every army, whether it stands and what      it holds, through every capture, whichever squares have been read or      folded yet (`UsingGameBoard-_fellIn`, `UsingGameBoard-_stakeOf`).

InvalidActionsPerReveal().details: Same class as a zero phase duration and refused in the same place:      it is a deployment mistake whose cost is the first player's stake      rather than a revert anybody sees.

InvalidCycleConfiguration().details: Both phases must be non-zero on a timed policy, and both must be      zero on a manual one. See {UsingCommitReveal} for why a zero phase      is not a configuration but a hole: it makes a commitment either      impossible to make or impossible to open.

InvalidFurtherActions(uint256,uint256).details: LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY. Without it a player dribbles one      action per transaction and spreads a turn across an unbounded number      of reveals, which is a denial of service on the reveal phase and on      everyone else's reads of the board. A chunk that promises a      successor must therefore be exactly full; only the LAST one may be      short.

InvalidPlayer(uint256).details: What makes an identity invalid is the GAME's, and it is decided in      one place: {UsingCommitReveal-_playerOf}. In the base's default,      an address identity, it means an id that is not an account, and in      a token game it means a token nobody has put at stake.

NextPhaseNotAllowed().details: A purely timed cycle needs no transaction at all - it simply is      what the clock says - so there is nothing for a caller to do here      and pretending otherwise would let one look like it had.

NoOneToWaitFor().details: Early advance needs a closed set of members. "Everyone has      committed" is not a question that can be answered under open      entry, and answering it against an empty set would let one caller      spin the cycle forward on their own.

NotInGame(uint256).details: What entering MEANS is the game's: a funded reserve here, custody of      a token elsewhere. What the cycle needs is only that the set of      players who may commit is the same set unanimity is measured      against - see {UsingCommitReveal-_makeCommitment}.

TooManyActions(uint256,uint256).details: The chunk is what makes a reveal's worst case CALCULABLE, on every      chain and whatever a game puts at stake, which is what lets a client      pass a real gas limit instead of a guess. A final chunk allowed to      be any length would give that back: the bound would hold for every      reveal except the last one of every turn.

params.commitmentHash: The head this reveal opened, which for the second        and later chunks of a turn is not the hash that was committed.
params.cost: What the game's resolution reported this chunk cost, taken        from the bond and from the reserve.
params.furtherActions: The new head, or zero when this completed the turn.

CommitmentVoid(uint256,uint64,bytes24,by.details: ONE EVENT FOR BOTH ROUTES, shaped like {CommitmentRevealed} because      a settlement shown the chunks walks the chain exactly as a reveal      does. A settlement WITHOUT them closes the commitment in one call      and reports a zero `furtherActions`.

params.commitmentHash: The head this settlement opened or closed.
params.cycleNumber: The cycle in progress when it was settled.
params.forfeited: How much the game's {UsingCommitReveal-_forfeit} took,        in the units of the bond. A game whose stake is not a bond (an        avatar in custody) reports zero here and says what it took in an        event of its own.
params.furtherActions: The new head, or zero when the commitment is now        closed and any surplus of its bond is reserve again.

CycleAdvanced(uint64,bool,address).details: A clock-driven turnover emits nothing, because nothing happened on      chain: that is the difference this event exists to make visible.

GameStarted(address,uint256,uint64).details: Followed by {CycleAdvanced} in the same transaction: starting      re-anchors the clock, so the first cycle runs its full length.

params.lastCycleNumber: The last cycle it plays: after it, the game has        ended.

params.gameOptions: What the game's own rules read at this table,        opaque to the base (see {UsingCommitReveal-_gameOptions}).

params.seated: How many seats are taken now.
How many seats are taken now.

params.waitedFor: Whether it now waits for them.
params.waitedForCount: How many members it waits for in total, which is        the denominator unanimity is measured against.

getArmiesOf(address).details: Every army is played by the account that created it.

isFrozen(uint256).details: A DEFINITION, NOT JUST A FLAG: an army landed on the board whose      missed reveal has been settled, OR which holds an unrevealed      commitment from a cycle that is over, so it is frozen from the      moment its reveal window closes, before anybody settles it. A      deployment never revealed is not frozen: it has no army to freeze,      and its stake is burned instead.

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.4;\n\nimport {StringUtils} from \"./utils/StringUtils.sol\";\nimport {SignatureUtils} from \"./utils/SignatureUtils.sol\";\n\n/// @title Delegation\n/// @notice Lets an account authorise other addresses to act in its name, at\n/// the contract that adopts this library and nowhere else.\n///\n/// The problem it solves: an app that acts on its user's behalf sends from a\n/// key of its own, so the address that signs a transaction is not the account\n/// the action belongs to. A contract that records `msg.sender` records the\n/// wrong one, and the user sees one address in the app and another against\n/// their actions, with nothing onchain connecting them.\n///\n/// THE UNIT OF AUTHORITY IS ONE CONTRACT: yours. A delegate authorised here may\n/// act for its owner here, and an identical signature is worth nothing at any\n/// other contract, because the contract's own address is part of what was\n/// signed. There is no scope, no capability and no per-route key: this library\n/// answers \"whose action is this\", which is identity, not permission. An\n/// adopter that needs narrower authority than \"the whole contract\" has a seam\n/// for it in {UsingDelegation-_requireAccountForSender}, which is more\n/// expressive than a storage key and costs nothing when unused.\n///\n/// A SET, NOT A SLOT: an owner may have any number of delegates at once, so a\n/// second front-end does not evict the first, and withdrawing one signer is not\n/// entangled with replacing another. The membership check costs exactly what an\n/// equality check did.\n///\n/// A LIBRARY, NOT A BASE CONTRACT, and deliberately. Inheriting would give a\n/// contract external functions that appear in its ABI without appearing in its\n/// source, which is the opposite of what a contract you are about to deploy\n/// should do, and it would stop an adopter declining a path it does not want.\n/// As a library neither applies: you write your own entry points, and you can\n/// see all of them.\n///\n/// The price is that you write those entry points, and they are lines that say\n/// exactly what your contract exposes. If the standard shape is what you want,\n/// {UsingDelegation} is that same set written once and ready to inherit - read\n/// it for the full set - and inheriting it is safe for the same reason this is\n/// a library at all, since the namespaced storage below means it declares no\n/// state and so shifts none of yours.\n///\n/// NOT A REGISTRY, and this is the one mistake that undoes everything above.\n/// \"A registry\" is the obvious noun for what this looks like, and a shared\n/// `DelegationRegistry` that many contracts point at is not a variation on this\n/// design, it is its opposite: the verifying contract in every signature would\n/// be that registry, so every credential granted for one game would be valid\n/// at every game on it, which is exactly the unbounded authority the contract\n/// field exists to remove. This package ships SOURCE. Each adopter compiles it\n/// into its own contract and owns its own delegations.\n///\n/// STORAGE IS NAMESPACED (ERC-7201), so this owns a region nothing else can\n/// collide with, at a slot derived from a name rather than from a position.\n/// A contract already live behind a proxy can therefore adopt delegation on an\n/// upgrade without disturbing the layout it already has.\n///\n/// Every function is `internal`, so they inline into your contract: no library\n/// deployment, no linking, no `delegatecall`, and `msg.sender` is still the\n/// caller you expect. It is also what makes `address(this)` in the signed text\n/// below mean YOUR contract rather than some library address.\nlibrary Delegation {\n    /// @notice the standing of one (owner, delegate) pair.\n    ///\n    /// The three states are exclusive, which is why one word per pair is\n    /// faithful rather than a compression of two flags: {revoke} sets\n    /// `Withdrawn` and removes authority in the same write, an owner-sent\n    /// {register} clears `Withdrawn` because it is a fresh decision, and the\n    /// signature path refuses to cross it.\n    ///\n    /// `None` is the zero value, so an untouched pair reads as no authority\n    /// without anything ever having been written.\n    enum Status {\n        None,\n        Allowed,\n        Withdrawn\n    }\n\n    /// @notice emitted whenever a (owner, delegate) pair changes standing.\n    ///\n    /// THIS EVENT IS THE ENUMERATION API. There is no onchain list of an\n    /// account's delegates - a linked set was costed and rejected, since few\n    /// delegates are expected and signer management belongs to the application\n    /// rather than to the library - so reconstructing the set means replaying\n    /// these logs in order. Both addresses are indexed, which gives a\n    /// per-account `eth_getLogs` query with no indexer; the flag is not, since\n    /// nobody filters on it.\n    ///\n    /// One event rather than an authorise/revoke pair, because a replay wants\n    /// both kinds in order and a single topic0 is one filter and one decode.\n    ///\n    /// The wart, and it belongs to the app rather than to this library: many\n    /// public and wallet-supplied RPCs cap `eth_getLogs` ranges, so a fresh\n    /// browser reconstructing from genesis needs a stored deployment block and\n    /// paging.\n    ///\n    /// @param owner the account being represented\n    /// @param delegate the address whose standing changed\n    /// @param allowed true when it may now act for `owner`, false when its\n    ///        authorisation was withdrawn\n    event DelegationChanged(\n        address indexed owner,\n        address indexed delegate,\n        bool allowed\n    );\n\n    /// @notice `sender` is not a delegate of `owner` at this contract\n    error NotDelegate(address owner, address sender);\n\n    /// @notice the owner withdrew its authorisation for `delegate`; only the\n    /// owner itself can authorise that delegate again (see {revoke})\n    error DelegationWithdrawn(address owner, address delegate);\n\n    /// @notice the signature was not produced by `owner`, or was produced for a\n    /// different delegate, deadline, contract or chain\n    error InvalidSignature();\n\n    /// @notice a delegate must be a real address; use {revoke} to withdraw one\n    error InvalidDelegate();\n\n    /// @notice the signature named a deadline that has already passed\n    error SignatureExpired(uint256 deadline);\n\n    /// @custom:storage-location erc7201:etherplay.storage.Delegation\n    struct Layout {\n        /// owner => delegate => whether that delegate may act for that owner\n        /// here, has been withdrawn, or was never authorised.\n        ///\n        /// Keyed by OWNER first, deliberately. The reverse mapping would let\n        /// anyone claim someone else's delegate address (which is public the\n        /// moment that delegate sends anything) and have that owner's actions\n        /// attributed to the claimer. Keyed this way, the worst an attacker\n        /// achieves is making their OWN account answer to an address they do\n        /// not control, which harms nobody.\n        ///\n        /// The inner key is the DELEGATE, so withdrawing one signer says\n        /// nothing about any other: a registration signature is permanently\n        /// derivable by whatever produced it, and a per-owner withdrawal would\n        /// make it impossible to add a new signer by signature alone once any\n        /// old one had been withdrawn.\n        mapping(address owner => mapping(address delegate => Status)) status;\n    }\n\n    /// keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"etherplay.storage.Delegation\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\n    bytes32 internal constant STORAGE_LOCATION =\n        0xe3a6fc8979f365f798ce92a5c63aa15935638389b80320c807252f142f884200;\n\n    /// @dev this library's storage, inside the CALLING contract.\n    ///\n    /// Internal library functions are inlined rather than `delegatecall`ed, so\n    /// the slot below resolves against the caller's own storage. That is what\n    /// lets a library own state without having any.\n    ///\n    /// PRIVATE, so an adopting contract cannot reach past the functions below\n    /// and write the mapping directly. `internal` would hand every adopter a\n    /// route around the zero-delegate check, the withdrawn state and the event,\n    /// which is a wide hole to leave in something meant to be handed to people\n    /// writing their own contracts. Nothing outside this library needs it.\n    function layout() private pure returns (Layout storage $) {\n        assembly {\n            $.slot := STORAGE_LOCATION\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // READING\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice the standing of one (owner, delegate) pair, as two flags.\n    ///\n    /// Two bools rather than the {Status} value itself, at the same single\n    /// SLOAD. It keeps an enum out of every interface, ABI and client that\n    /// would otherwise have to remember whether 2 means withdrawn, and both\n    /// questions an app has - may this signer act, and do I need a transaction\n    /// from the owner to fix it - are answered by one call.\n    ///\n    /// @return allowed whether `delegate` may act for `owner` here\n    /// @return withdrawn whether `owner` withdrew `delegate`, which blocks\n    ///         {registerViaSignature} for that delegate until `owner`\n    ///         authorises it again itself\n    function statusOf(\n        address owner,\n        address delegate\n    ) internal view returns (bool allowed, bool withdrawn) {\n        Status current = layout().status[owner][delegate];\n        return (current == Status.Allowed, current == Status.Withdrawn);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice whether `sender` may act as `onBehalfOf`.\n    ///\n    /// Asks; does not enforce. For a view a UI can call before offering an\n    /// action, and for a call site that wants to do something other than revert.\n    /// Anyone may always act as themselves, and a zero `onBehalfOf` means\n    /// exactly that, so neither costs an SLOAD.\n    ///\n    /// @param sender normally `msg.sender`, but see UsingDelegation for the\n    ///        case where a contract resolves its effective sender differently\n    /// @param onBehalfOf the account being claimed, or zero for none\n    function canActFor(\n        address sender,\n        address onBehalfOf\n    ) internal view returns (bool) {\n        if (onBehalfOf == address(0) || onBehalfOf == sender) {\n            return true;\n        }\n        return layout().status[onBehalfOf][sender] == Status.Allowed;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice the account this action belongs to, or revert.\n    ///\n    /// THE FUNCTION YOUR CONTRACT ACTUALLY USES. Call it wherever you would\n    /// have taken `msg.sender` as the identity an action belongs to, and record\n    /// what it returns. A zero `onBehalfOf` means \"acting for myself\", so an\n    /// entry point can pass one through unconditionally and behave exactly as\n    /// it did before delegation existed.\n    ///\n    /// NAMED FOR THE ENFORCEMENT, not just the lookup: it reverts on an\n    /// unauthorised claim rather than falling back to the sender. Somebody\n    /// trying to act as somebody else is not a request to act as themselves,\n    /// and quietly recording it that way would store an action nobody asked\n    /// for. Use {canActFor} when a question rather than a requirement is what\n    /// you want.\n    ///\n    /// @param sender normally `msg.sender`, but see UsingDelegation for the\n    ///        case where a contract resolves its effective sender differently\n    /// @param onBehalfOf the account being claimed, or zero for none\n    function requireAccountFor(\n        address sender,\n        address onBehalfOf\n    ) internal view returns (address) {\n        if (!canActFor(sender, onBehalfOf)) {\n            revert NotDelegate(onBehalfOf, sender);\n        }\n        return onBehalfOf == address(0) ? sender : onBehalfOf;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // GRANTING\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice authorise `delegate` to act for `owner` here, on `owner`'s own\n    /// say-so.\n    ///\n    /// AUTHORISES NOTHING ITSELF: the adopting contract must already have\n    /// established that `owner` is the one asking, normally by passing\n    /// `msg.sender`. It also CLEARS a previous withdrawal of `delegate`, which\n    /// is only sound BECAUSE the owner is acting directly - that is a fresh\n    /// decision, not a signature presented again - so passing anything else\n    /// here would let one account undo another's revocation.\n    ///\n    /// @param owner the account authorising, i.e. `msg.sender`\n    /// @param delegate the address to authorise; use {revoke} to withdraw it\n    function register(address owner, address delegate) internal {\n        if (delegate == address(0)) {\n            revert InvalidDelegate();\n        }\n        layout().status[owner][delegate] = Status.Allowed;\n        emit DelegationChanged(owner, delegate, true);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice authorise `delegate` to act for `owner` here, proven by\n    /// `owner`'s signature, whoever is sending the transaction.\n    ///\n    /// The point: an owner that can sign but cannot send, or that holds no\n    /// funds, can still delegate. It signs, somebody else submits and pays.\n    ///\n    /// The signature carries no nonce, on purpose. It grants a standing\n    /// authorisation to one named address at one named contract on one named\n    /// chain, so presenting it a second time only re-asserts what is already\n    /// true, at the submitter's expense. The one thing repetition could undo is\n    /// a revocation, which is why {revoke} leaves a state this refuses to cross\n    /// for THAT delegate only - a different delegate can still be authorised by\n    /// a fresh signature.\n    ///\n    /// WHAT IS AND IS NOT CALLER-SUPPLIED. The contract and the chain come from\n    /// `address(this)` and `block.chainid` and can never be passed in, because\n    /// they are the bounds the whole design rests on and a caller-supplied\n    /// bound is no bound at all. The deadline HAS to be passed in: it was\n    /// chosen by whoever produced the signature and this contract has no other\n    /// way to learn it. That is safe because it is not trusted - a deadline\n    /// that does not match the one that was signed simply recovers a different\n    /// address, and lying about it in either direction fails, since a later\n    /// deadline breaks the signature and an earlier one only expires sooner.\n    ///\n    /// THE OWNER MUST BE A KEY, not a contract. Verification is `ecrecover`, so\n    /// an ERC-1271 smart account cannot register this way and there is no\n    /// `isValidSignature` fallback. Such an account is not locked out, it takes\n    /// the other path: {register}, which proves who is asking by who is sending.\n    /// The two suit opposite shapes, and this one exists for a signer that can\n    /// sign and cannot send, which is the thing a contract account is not.\n    ///\n    /// WHAT THE DEADLINE BOUNDS is how long the credential may be PRESENTED,\n    /// not how long the authority lasts. Once registered, a delegate stands\n    /// until it is revoked. That is the honest reading of a standing\n    /// authorisation, and it is why a deadline is worth having anyway: it is\n    /// the only bound on a credential that was minted without a human in the\n    /// loop and has since turned out to be a mistake.\n    ///\n    /// @param owner the account being represented\n    /// @param delegate the address to authorise\n    /// @param deadline the unix time after which this signature stops being\n    ///        accepted, or zero for no expiry\n    /// @param signature `owner`'s signature over {message}\n    function registerViaSignature(\n        address owner,\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline,\n        bytes calldata signature\n    ) internal {\n        if (delegate == address(0)) {\n            revert InvalidDelegate();\n        }\n        if (deadline != 0 && block.timestamp > deadline) {\n            revert SignatureExpired(deadline);\n        }\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        if ($.status[owner][delegate] == Status.Withdrawn) {\n            revert DelegationWithdrawn(owner, delegate);\n        }\n        if (\n            SignatureUtils.recover(digest(delegate, deadline), signature) !=\n            owner\n        ) {\n            revert InvalidSignature();\n        }\n\n        $.status[owner][delegate] = Status.Allowed;\n        emit DelegationChanged(owner, delegate, true);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice withdraw `owner`'s authorisation of `delegate`: it can no longer\n    /// act here, and no signature can put THAT delegate back.\n    ///\n    /// AUTHORISES NOTHING ITSELF: the adopting contract must already have\n    /// established that `owner` is the one asking, normally by passing\n    /// `msg.sender`.\n    ///\n    /// Takes the delegate as an argument, because an owner may have several and\n    /// \"withdraw everything\" is not what someone replacing one signer means.\n    /// Withdrawing an address that was never authorised is allowed and is not a\n    /// no-op: it pre-empts a signature that may already exist for it, which is a\n    /// real case, since a credential is derivable by whatever produced it long\n    /// before anyone submits it.\n    ///\n    /// The zero delegate is the one exception, and is refused. Neither register\n    /// path can ever have accepted it, so there is nothing to withdraw and no\n    /// signature to pre-empt: it can only be a caller passing an address it\n    /// failed to set. Refusing costs one comparison and keeps a meaningless\n    /// entry out of {DelegationChanged}, which matters more than it sounds,\n    /// because that log IS the enumeration API and an app replaying it would\n    /// have to know to ignore the entry.\n    ///\n    /// One-way as far as signatures are concerned, deliberately. Re-authorising\n    /// the SAME delegate takes a transaction from the owner ({register}),\n    /// because a signature that carries no nonce can state a standing\n    /// authorisation but cannot express a decision to reverse one, and reading\n    /// it as such would let an old signature outrank a newer intent. A DIFFERENT\n    /// delegate can still be authorised by a fresh signature.\n    ///\n    /// This is withdrawal of consent, not key rotation. If a delegate key leaks\n    /// there is nothing to rotate to that the same leak would not also expose,\n    /// so the useful response is to stop.\n    function revoke(address owner, address delegate) internal {\n        if (delegate == address(0)) {\n            revert InvalidDelegate();\n        }\n        layout().status[owner][delegate] = Status.Withdrawn;\n        emit DelegationChanged(owner, delegate, false);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // THE SIGNED TEXT\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    // Prose, then a block of labelled fields.\n    //\n    // Readable text rather than typed data, because the owner is being asked to\n    // hand another address authority over their account, and what they can read\n    // in the signing dialog matters more than what it costs to check here. The\n    // shape borrows from EIP-4361 without being it: 4361 is built around a\n    // domain, a URI and a nonce, all three deliberately absent here.\n    //\n    // The prose comes FIRST so the first thing a human sees is what they are\n    // agreeing to, and so the field block cannot be mistaken for the leading\n    // `Origin:` line of the etherplay convention, which tells a conforming\n    // wallet a message is safe to sign without asking. It is not: a wallet\n    // implementing only that rule must fall through to prompting.\n    //\n    // EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS IS A FIELD, none of it inline in the prose,\n    // because a wallet has to extract the delegate (to compare against the\n    // signer it derives) and the contract and chain (to check against whatever\n    // it auto-signs), and one extraction strategy is better than two.\n    //\n    // There is no origin in it. The wallet always knows the true origin of the\n    // page asking, so a claimed one tells it nothing, and the delegate address\n    // already carries the origin binding by being a pure function of (account\n    // key, origin). There is no version field either: any change to these bytes\n    // invalidates every signature regardless, so there is no negotiation to be\n    // had, and a wallet that cannot parse what it sees falls back to showing\n    // raw text and prompting.\n    //\n    // `Expires: never` stays a line rather than being omitted, since an absent\n    // line is easy for a human to miss and easy for a parser to treat as an\n    // unset default.\n    //\n    // WHATEVER PRODUCES THE SIGNATURE BUILDS THIS SAME STRING, so the wording,\n    // the field order and the address casing are consensus, not style. Changing\n    // any of it invalidates every signature ever generated, silently. The other\n    // implementations in this package are the TypeScript builder in `src/` and\n    // the ABI it is exercised through; all of them are pinned against\n    // `vectors.json`, and a change to one without the others is a change that\n    // will pass review and fail in production.\n    string internal constant MESSAGE_HEAD =\n        \"IMPORTANT: Only sign this on a site you trust.\\n\\n\"\n        \"This authorizes another address to act in your name onchain, at one contract.\\n\"\n        \"You can withdraw it at any time by revoking it there.\\n\\n\"\n        \"Delegate: \";\n    string internal constant MESSAGE_CONTRACT = \"\\nContract: \";\n    string internal constant MESSAGE_CHAIN_ID = \"\\nChain ID: \";\n    string internal constant MESSAGE_EXPIRES = \"\\nExpires: \";\n    string internal constant MESSAGE_NO_EXPIRY = \"never\";\n\n    /// @notice the exact text an owner signs to authorise `delegate` here.\n    ///\n    /// Expose it, so a caller can display it and so whatever produces the\n    /// signature can be asserted byte-for-byte against it. The two have to\n    /// agree exactly or every signature is rejected, so the agreement is worth\n    /// being checkable from outside rather than by reading both sides.\n    ///\n    /// `view` rather than `pure`: the contract and the chain are read from\n    /// `address(this)` and `block.chainid` rather than taken as arguments,\n    /// which is what stops a caller choosing them.\n    ///\n    /// Both addresses are rendered lowercase; see {StringUtils-toHexString}.\n    /// The deadline is decimal unix seconds, or the word `never` for zero.\n    ///\n    /// BUILT IN TWO PARTS, AND IT HAS TO BE. Do not fold these back into one\n    /// `abi.encodePacked`, however much it wants to be one: with the optimizer\n    /// ENABLED, solc 0.8.28 encodes a packed tuple through a generated Yul\n    /// block that holds every argument on the stack at once, and at seven or\n    /// more dynamic arguments that block is stack-too-deep before any of this\n    /// library's own locals are counted. Eight arguments is what the fields\n    /// below come to, so the single-call form does not compile under any\n    /// optimizer setting at all - not at low `runs`, not at `runs: 1` - while\n    /// compiling fine with the optimizer off, which is the reverse of the usual\n    /// stack-too-deep and the reason this looks like a rewrite of working code.\n    /// Six arguments is the last that fits, so the field block is encoded on\n    /// its own and the prose is prepended to it.\n    ///\n    /// THE BYTES ARE UNCHANGED BY THE SPLIT. Every piece here is a `string`, so\n    /// packed encoding is plain concatenation with no length prefix and no\n    /// padding, and concatenation is associative: `A | (B | C)` is `A | B | C`.\n    /// `vectors.json` is what actually holds that claim down.\n    function message(\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline\n    ) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        bytes memory fields = abi.encodePacked(\n            MESSAGE_CONTRACT,\n            StringUtils.toHexString(address(this)),\n            MESSAGE_CHAIN_ID,\n            StringUtils.toString(block.chainid),\n            MESSAGE_EXPIRES,\n            deadline == 0 ? MESSAGE_NO_EXPIRY : StringUtils.toString(deadline)\n        );\n        return\n            string(\n                abi.encodePacked(\n                    MESSAGE_HEAD,\n                    StringUtils.toHexString(delegate),\n                    fields\n                )\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice the EIP-191 digest of {message}.\n    function digest(\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline\n    ) internal view returns (bytes32) {\n        return SignatureUtils.textDigest(bytes(message(delegate, deadline)));\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x61e6d6e0a3d422a2d09728705c0304a1a788dcb4f2236b18897b84bf9c3e2230","license":"MIT"},"npm/@etherplay/delegation@0.1.2/contracts/IDelegation.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.4;\n\n/// @title IDelegation\n/// @notice The delegation entry points as a type, for code that has to NAME\n/// them rather than inherit them.\n///\n/// {UsingDelegation} already writes these functions, so a contract that\n/// inherits it needs nothing from here. This exists for the cases where the\n/// implementation is not the thing being described:\n///\n///  - A contract behind a ROUTER cannot say \"these selectors are mine\" by\n///    inheriting an abstract contract: the router needs a list of selectors,\n///    composed from interfaces, while the implementation lives elsewhere.\n///    Without a shared declaration every router restates the same six\n///    signatures, and a restatement is a copy that can drift.\n///  - A client, a script or a test that calls into a contract it does not\n///    compile against - `IDelegation(target).delegationStatus(owner, delegate)`\n///    - which is also the shape the TypeScript side of this package exports as\n///    `DELEGATION_ABI`, checked against this file by a test.\n///\n/// DO NOT WRITE `is IDelegation, UsingDelegation`. It does not compile without\n/// restating all six functions as `override`, which is exactly the boilerplate\n/// {UsingDelegation} exists to spare an adopter. Inherit the implementation\n/// alone and use this interface where a TYPE is wanted; the two agreeing is\n/// covered by a test (test/solidity/IDelegation.t.sol), and on a router the\n/// thing that actually breaks is a selector that does not route - a missing\n/// route in the deploy script, or two routes claiming the same selector - which\n/// no compiler check would have caught.\n///\n/// The whole external surface, in the order {UsingDelegation} declares it, so\n/// the two can be read side by side.\n///\n/// There is no `delegateOf`. An account may have several delegates, so no\n/// single address could be returned without being a lie, and the set is\n/// reconstructed from `DelegationChanged` logs rather than read. Every caller\n/// only ever asked about a pair anyway.\ninterface IDelegation {\n    /// @notice authorise `delegate` to act for you here, and optionally fund it.\n    function registerDelegate(\n        address delegate,\n        address payable payee\n    ) external payable;\n\n    /// @notice authorise `delegate` to act for `owner` here, proven by `owner`'s\n    /// signature, and fund that delegate with whatever value is sent.\n    function registerDelegateViaSignature(\n        address owner,\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline,\n        bytes calldata signature\n    ) external payable;\n\n    /// @notice withdraw your authorisation of `delegate`; no signature can put\n    /// that one back.\n    function revokeDelegate(address delegate) external;\n\n    /// @notice whether `delegate` may act for `owner` here, and whether `owner`\n    /// withdrew it.\n    function delegationStatus(\n        address owner,\n        address delegate\n    ) external view returns (bool allowed, bool withdrawn);\n\n    /// @notice the exact text an owner signs to authorise `delegate` here.\n    function delegationMessage(\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline\n    ) external view returns (string memory);\n\n    /// @notice the EIP-191 digest of {delegationMessage}.\n    function delegationDigest(\n        address delegate,\n        uint256 deadline\n    ) external view returns (bytes32);\n}\n","keccak256":"0xf6ab344b72ea9a0714867c0044d3505cbcf2d1029afd8b92b578afc0b60c93d6","license":"MIT"},"npm/@etherplay/delegation@0.1.2/contracts/utils/SignatureUtils.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.4;\n\nimport {StringUtils} from \"./StringUtils.sol\";\n\n/// @title Signature Utils\n/// @notice Recovering the address behind a signature, with the checks\n/// `ecrecover` does not do for you.\n///\n/// A library of `internal` functions, so it inlines into its callers and costs\n/// nothing to deploy. It holds no state.\nlibrary SignatureUtils {\n    /// @notice the signature is not 65 bytes, or carries values no honest\n    /// signer produces\n    error MalformedSignature();\n\n    /// @notice the signature is well-formed but recovers to nobody\n    error UnrecoverableSignature();\n\n    /// @notice the address that produced `signature` over `digest`.\n    ///\n    /// `ecrecover` alone is not enough, and each of the three checks here exists\n    /// for a distinct reason:\n    ///\n    /// - A length other than 65 means the caller passed something that is not a\n    ///   signature at all, and reading past it would recover an address from\n    ///   whatever happened to be in memory.\n    /// - The curve is symmetric, so `(r, s)` and `(r, -s)` both recover the same\n    ///   address. Accepting either turns one authorisation into two distinct\n    ///   valid signatures, which breaks anything that identifies a signature by\n    ///   its bytes. Only the low half is accepted.\n    /// - `ecrecover` returns the zero address on failure rather than reverting,\n    ///   so an unchecked result compares equal to an uninitialised mapping entry\n    ///   and quietly authorises the wrong thing.\n    ///\n    /// `v` IS DELIBERATELY NOT CANONICALISED, and that qualifies the second\n    /// point above rather than extending it. Both encodings in circulation are\n    /// accepted - the 27/28 of `eth_sign` and the raw 0/1 recovery bit - because\n    /// signers genuinely differ on which they emit, and refusing half of them\n    /// buys nothing. So one authorisation does still have two accepted byte\n    /// strings, differing in the last byte. That is safe HERE because nothing in\n    /// this package identifies a signature by its bytes: the withdrawn state is\n    /// keyed by (owner, delegate), and a credential presented twice only\n    /// re-asserts what is already true. A caller that DOES key on signature\n    /// bytes has to normalise `v` itself before doing so.\n    ///\n    /// @param digest what was signed\n    /// @param signature 65 bytes, `r || s || v`\n    /// @return the recovered address, never the zero address\n    function recover(\n        bytes32 digest,\n        bytes calldata signature\n    ) internal pure returns (address) {\n        if (signature.length != 65) {\n            revert MalformedSignature();\n        }\n\n        bytes32 r;\n        bytes32 s;\n        uint8 v;\n        assembly {\n            r := calldataload(signature.offset)\n            s := calldataload(add(signature.offset, 32))\n            v := byte(0, calldataload(add(signature.offset, 64)))\n        }\n\n        // secp256k1n / 2\n        if (\n            uint256(s) >\n            0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF5D576E7357A4501DDFE92F46681B20A0\n        ) {\n            revert MalformedSignature();\n        }\n        if (v < 27) {\n            v += 27;\n        }\n        if (v != 27 && v != 28) {\n            revert MalformedSignature();\n        }\n\n        address signer = ecrecover(digest, v, r, s);\n        if (signer == address(0)) {\n            revert UnrecoverableSignature();\n        }\n        return signer;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice the EIP-191 `personal_sign` digest of a text message.\n    ///\n    /// What a wallet actually signs when asked to sign a string: the text with\n    /// a fixed prefix and its own byte length in front, so a signature over a\n    /// message can never be replayed as a signature over a transaction.\n    ///\n    /// The length is decimal ASCII, which is why this needs {StringUtils}.\n    ///\n    /// @param message the exact bytes shown to the signer\n    function textDigest(bytes memory message) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return\n            keccak256(\n                abi.encodePacked(\n                    \"\\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\\n\",\n                    StringUtils.toString(message.length),\n                    message\n                )\n            );\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xd5e4eaa778e90324f88a7f5cb50bed66ce7eb1ca7ba0105f42a99e27de63ee97","license":"MIT"},"npm/@etherplay/delegation@0.1.2/contracts/utils/StringUtils.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.4;\n\n/// @title String Utils\n/// @notice Rendering values as text.\n///\n/// Needed wherever a contract has to reproduce a string that was built\n/// somewhere else, which in practice means verifying a signature over\n/// human-readable text: the signed bytes only match if both sides spell the\n/// values the same way.\n///\n/// A library of `internal` functions, so it is inlined into its callers and\n/// costs nothing to deploy. It holds no state and knows nothing about who uses\n/// it.\nlibrary StringUtils {\n    bytes internal constant HEX_DIGITS = \"0123456789abcdef\";\n\n    /// @notice `0x`-prefixed, LOWERCASE hex form of an address.\n    ///\n    /// Lowercase rather than EIP-55 checksummed, deliberately. Checksumming\n    /// costs a hash of the lowercase form plus a pass over every character, and\n    /// settles nothing that matters: whoever produces a signature and whoever\n    /// verifies it must agree on one spelling regardless, so the useful property\n    /// is that the spelling is unambiguous and cheap, not that it carries a\n    /// typo-detecting checksum nobody in this path is reading.\n    ///\n    /// The other implementations of the delegation message therefore have to\n    /// lowercase too, and the vectors file carries checksummed inputs precisely\n    /// to catch one that forgot.\n    ///\n    /// @param value the address to render\n    /// @return the 42-character lowercase representation\n    function toHexString(address value) internal pure returns (string memory) {\n        bytes20 raw = bytes20(value);\n        bytes memory result = new bytes(42);\n        result[0] = \"0\";\n        result[1] = \"x\";\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < 20; i++) {\n            result[2 + i * 2] = HEX_DIGITS[uint8(raw[i]) >> 4];\n            result[3 + i * 2] = HEX_DIGITS[uint8(raw[i]) & 0x0f];\n        }\n        return string(result);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice decimal form of a number.\n    ///\n    /// @param value the number to render\n    /// @return the shortest representation, with no leading zero except for\n    ///         zero itself\n    function toString(uint256 value) internal pure returns (string memory) {\n        if (value == 0) {\n            return \"0\";\n        }\n        uint256 digits;\n        for (uint256 rest = value; rest != 0; rest /= 10) {\n            digits++;\n        }\n        bytes memory buffer = new bytes(digits);\n        while (value != 0) {\n            digits--;\n            buffer[digits] = bytes1(uint8(48 + (value % 10)));\n            value /= 10;\n        }\n        return string(buffer);\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x605f5db1064e404b670349cd4810256dead251effa723cc31c39393446fe84fa","license":"MIT"},"npm/solidity-kit@0.5.7/solc_0_8/ERC20/interfaces/IERC20.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nimport \"./UsingERC20Events.sol\";\n\ninterface IERC20 is UsingERC20Events {\n    /// @notice Returns the total token supply.\n    function totalSupply() external view returns (uint256);\n\n    /// @notice Returns the number of decimals the token uses.\n    function decimals() external view returns (uint8);\n\n    /// @notice Returns the symbol of the token.\n    function symbol() external view returns (string memory);\n\n    /// @notice Returns the name of the token.\n    function name() external view returns (string memory);\n\n    /// @notice Returns the account balance of another account with address `owner`.\n    function balanceOf(address owner) external view returns (uint256);\n\n    /// @notice Transfers `amount` of tokens to address `to`.\n    function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool);\n\n    /// @notice Returns the amount which `spender` is still allowed to withdraw from `owner`.\n    function allowance(address owner, address spender) external view returns (uint256);\n\n    /// @notice Allows `spender` to withdraw from your account multiple times, up to `amount`.\n    function approve(address spender, uint256 amount) external returns (bool);\n\n    /// @notice Transfers `amount` tokens from address `from` to address `to`.\n    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool);\n}\n","keccak256":"0x3a6bcd5cf1d9e50fbe405f4c6c9c868e97ce2a84ae99fd7c1fb2d916c4d5debd","license":"MIT"},"npm/solidity-kit@0.5.7/solc_0_8/ERC20/interfaces/UsingERC20Events.sol":{"content":"// account the tokens are sent from\n    /// @param to the account the tokens are sent to\n    /// @param value number of tokens sent\n    event Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value);\n\n    /// @notice trigger on approval amount being set.\n    ///   Note that Transfer events need to be considered to compute the current allowance.\n    /// @param owner the account approving the `spender`\n    /// @param spender the account allowed to spend\n    /// @param value the amount granted\n    event Approval(address indexed owner, address indexed spender, uint256 value);\n}\n","keccak256":"0x15eaa1de7fe9e02ba9e83f262b2b7f33a4bfe0f5a3ae2be4d616b6c4dce1c6fa","license":"MIT"},"npm/solidity-kit@0.5.7/solc_0_8/debug/time/interfaces/ITime.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\nimport \"./UsingTimeEvents.sol\";\n\ninterface ITime is UsingTimeEvents {\n    function timestamp() external view returns (uint256);\n}\n\ninterface ITimeSetter is UsingTimeEvents {\n    function increaseTime(uint256 delta) external;\n}\n","keccak256":"0xa81ea4359b841652e020f83fded0488b2df8409ebaaf2c39362f2ef4bdb454e9","license":"MIT"},"npm/solidity-kit@0.5.7/solc_0_8/debug/time/interfaces/UsingTimeEvents.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\ninterface UsingTimeEvents {\n    event TimeIncreased(uint256 newTime, uint256 delta);\n}\n","keccak256":"0x73ca9f6cce68bd84d1d487bb3e7bbe4224ab413bc4007ff4a22e0abb04897de4","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/CommitReveal.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealTypes as T} from \"./interfaces/UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol\";\nimport {UsingCommitRevealEvents as Ev} from \"./interfaces/UsingCommitRevealEvents.sol\";\nimport {UsingCommitRevealErrors as E} from \"./interfaces/UsingCommitRevealErrors.sol\";\n\n/// @title CommitReveal\n/// @notice The commit-reveal mechanism every game on this template shares: a\n///         reserve, a bonded commitment that is the head of a hash chain of\n///         chunks, the cycle and its policies, who the cycle waits for, and the\n///         two ways a missed reveal is settled.\n///\n/// A LIBRARY OVER NAMESPACED STORAGE, the shape of the etherplay delegation\n/// package's `Delegation`, and for the same reasons. Every function is `internal`, so it\n/// inlines into the calling contract: no deployment, no linking, `msg.sender`\n/// is the caller you expect. And the state lives at an ERC-7201 slot derived\n/// from a name, so it collides with nothing a game declares and every route\n/// behind a router reads the same record without sharing a base contract's\n/// layout.\n///\n/// IT KNOWS NOTHING OF A GAME'S ACTIONS. A game's routes stay typed; the game\n/// computes the commitment digest over its own action type and hands this\n/// library the digest and the number of actions. What the library checks is\n/// that the digest is the head of the chain and that the chunk has a lawful\n/// length; what it charges is what the game's resolution REPORTS. See\n/// {UsingCommitReveal-_openChunk} for the pair a game calls around its\n/// resolution.\n///\n/// IT CALLS NO SEAM. Who the caller acts for, what a missed reveal costs and\n/// where the cycle is are a game's answers, so they are virtual functions on\n/// {UsingCommitReveal}; a library cannot call a virtual function, and the\n/// split falls exactly there. A game that wants none of the convenience\n/// contract can call this directly and supply its own.\nlibrary CommitReveal {\n    /// @notice The clock a cycle is read off, as the convenience contract\n    ///         holds it in immutables.\n    struct Clock {\n        T.CyclePolicy policy;\n        uint256 startTime;\n        uint256 commitPhaseDuration;\n        uint256 revealPhaseDuration;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice A chunk that has been CHECKED and not yet applied.\n    /// @dev Returned by {openChunk} and {openMissedChunk}, consumed by\n    ///      {closeRevealedChunk} and {closeMissedChunk}. Opening writes nothing,\n    ///      closing writes everything: a game that opened a chunk and forgot to\n    ///      close it has not advanced the chain, has not been charged and has\n    ///      not counted the turn, so its reveal visibly does not complete.\n    struct Chunk {\n        uint256 player;\n        /// @notice the cycle in progress when the chunk was opened\n        uint64 cycleNumber;\n        /// @notice the head the chunk opened\n        bytes24 commitmentHash;\n        /// @notice the head it leaves behind, zero for the last chunk\n        bytes24 furtherActions;\n        /// @notice opened as a settlement of a missed reveal, not as a reveal\n        bool missed;\n    }\n\n    /// @custom:storage-location erc7201:etherplay.storage.CommitReveal\n    struct Layout {\n        /// @notice Tokens a player puts at risk in order to play, keyed by\n        ///         WHO PLAYS, which is a number and never an address.\n        mapping(uint256 player => uint256 amount) reserve;\n        mapping(uint256 player => T.Commitment commitment) commitments;\n        /// @notice What the last advance wrote down.\n        T.CycleState cycleState;\n        /// @notice How many of the members have acted in the cycle it names.\n        T.CycleTally tally;\n        /// @notice How many members the cycle waits for: the denominator of\n        ///         unanimity.\n        uint64 waitedFor;\n        /// @notice Whether this player is one of them, so the count cannot be\n        ///         incremented twice for the same member.\n        mapping(uint256 player => bool) isWaitedFor;\n        /// @notice A closed roster, if one was opened; all zero is open entry.\n        /// @dev Appended, so a layout written before rosters existed reads it\n        ///      as open entry.\n        T.Roster roster;\n        /// @notice Who holds a seat, in no particular order.\n        uint256[] members;\n        /// @notice Where a member is in {members}, plus one; zero is unseated.\n        mapping(uint256 player => uint256 indexPlusOne) seatOf;\n        /// @notice What a game's own rules read at this table, set with its\n        ///         roster and never again; the base does not interpret it.\n        /// @dev Appended, for the same reason as {roster}.\n        bytes32 gameOptions;\n    }\n\n    /// keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"etherplay.storage.CommitReveal\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\n    bytes32 internal constant STORAGE_LOCATION =\n        0xadc5f43ba75b96408298ed0e334b2a1fd450d7199af4cc31fa65c6246d8b9300;\n\n    /// @dev PRIVATE, so a game cannot write a commitment or a reserve except\n    ///      through the functions below, which are where the rules are.\n    function layout() private pure returns (Layout storage $) {\n        assembly {\n            $.slot := STORAGE_LOCATION\n        }\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // RESERVE\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function reserveOf(uint256 player) internal view returns (uint256) {\n        return layout().reserve[player];\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Credit a player's reserve. Moving the tokens is the caller's.\n    function deposit(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (uint256 newAmount) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        newAmount = $.reserve[player] + amount;\n        $.reserve[player] = newAmount;\n        emit Ev.ReserveDeposited(player, amount, newAmount);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Debit a player's reserve on their own request.\n    /// @dev What is bonded to an open commitment cannot be withdrawn, or a\n    ///      player could commit, see the cycle turn against them, and pull\n    ///      their stake out instead of revealing.\n    ///\n    ///      AND YOU CANNOT EMPTY IT WITH A TURN STILL OPEN, which is the same\n    ///      rule applied to what is really at stake. A turn bonding ZERO locks\n    ///      nothing, so without this a player could commit, empty their\n    ///      reserve, cease to be waited for (where membership is a funded\n    ///      reserve), and leave the cycle counting their commitment while no\n    ///      longer counting them - at which point a SUBSET satisfies unanimity\n    ///      and closes the phase on somebody who has not acted. An idle\n    ///      player's automatic empty turn bonds exactly zero.\n    function withdraw(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (uint256 newAmount) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        uint256 current = $.reserve[player];\n\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = $.commitments[player];\n        uint256 locked = commitment.cycleNumber == 0 ? 0 : commitment.bond;\n\n        if (amount + locked > current) {\n            revert E.ReserveTooLow(current, amount + locked);\n        }\n        if (amount == current && commitment.cycleNumber != 0) {\n            revert E.CommitmentStillOpen(commitment.cycleNumber);\n        }\n\n        newAmount = current - amount;\n        $.reserve[player] = newAmount;\n        emit Ev.ReserveWithdrawn(player, amount, newAmount);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Take up to `amount` out of a player's reserve, and say how much.\n    /// @dev No event of its own: the caller is a settlement, which reports\n    ///      what it took in {UsingCommitRevealEvents-CommitmentVoid}.\n    function debit(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (uint256 taken) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        uint256 current = $.reserve[player];\n        taken = amount > current ? current : amount;\n        $.reserve[player] = current - taken;\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // WHO THE CYCLE WAITS FOR\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function isWaitedFor(uint256 player) internal view returns (bool) {\n        return layout().isWaitedFor[player];\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Start blocking the cycle on this player.\n    /// @dev Idempotent on purpose: the caller is a game rule (\"a funded\n    ///      reserve means you are in\", \"an avatar in custody is in\") and rules\n    ///      fire more than once. A count that could be incremented twice for\n    ///      one member would make unanimity unreachable, which is a deadlock\n    ///      rather than an error message.\n    function startWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        if ($.isWaitedFor[player]) {\n            return;\n        }\n        $.isWaitedFor[player] = true;\n        uint64 count = $.waitedFor + 1;\n        $.waitedFor = count;\n        emit Ev.WaitedForChanged(player, true, count);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Stop blocking the cycle on this player.\n    /// @dev The whole of what leaving means. It settles nothing, returns\n    ///      nothing and burns nothing, because those are the GAME's questions\n    ///      and answering them here would make \"stop waiting for me\" into a\n    ///      costless exit from a commitment - which is the one thing this\n    ///      template may never offer. Idempotent for the same reason as\n    ///      {startWaitingFor}: a game that drops a member on forfeit AND on\n    ///      withdrawal has two callers, and a count that fell below the members\n    ///      who can answer would let a subset satisfy \"unanimity\".\n    function stopWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        if (!$.isWaitedFor[player]) {\n            return;\n        }\n        $.isWaitedFor[player] = false;\n        uint64 count = $.waitedFor - 1;\n        $.waitedFor = count;\n        emit Ev.WaitedForChanged(player, false, count);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The denominator, and how much of it has acted in this cycle.\n    function attendance(\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (T.Attendance memory result) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        result.waitedFor = $.waitedFor;\n        T.CycleTally memory tally = $.tally;\n        if (tally.cycleNumber == cycleNumber) {\n            result.committed = tally.committed;\n            result.revealed = tally.revealed;\n        }\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // A CLOSED ROSTER\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function roster() internal view returns (T.Roster memory) {\n        return layout().roster;\n    }\n\n    function members() internal view returns (uint256[] memory) {\n        return layout().members;\n    }\n\n    function isSeated(uint256 player) internal view returns (bool) {\n        return layout().seatOf[player] != 0;\n    }\n\n    function gameOptions() internal view returns (bytes32) {\n        return layout().gameOptions;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The last cycle this game plays, or zero if it has no end (open\n    ///         entry, or a roster not started yet).\n    function lastCycleNumber() internal view returns (uint64) {\n        return layout().cycleState.lastCycleNumber;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Whether `cycleNumber` is past the last cycle this game plays.\n    function isPastTheEnd(uint64 cycleNumber) internal view returns (bool) {\n        uint64 last = layout().cycleState.lastCycleNumber;\n        return last != 0 && cycleNumber > last;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Give a game a closed roster. Once, and before anyone joined.\n    /// @param cycles How many cycles it plays from its start: at least one,\n    ///        since a game for a fixed set of members that never ends can\n    ///        never name a winner.\n    /// @param options What the GAME reads at this table (a stake, a board's\n    ///        size), stored here because a game's route cannot be called from\n    ///        the lobby's: see {UsingCommitReveal-_gameOptions}.\n    /// @dev A ROSTER IS A WHOLE MODE, NOT A SETTING: who the cycle waits for\n    ///      starts as nobody and becomes the members only when the creator\n    ///      starts the game, so a game cannot switch to it once open entry has\n    ///      let somebody in.\n    function openRoster(\n        address creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 options\n    ) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        if ($.roster.seats != 0) {\n            revert E.RosterAlreadyOpened();\n        }\n        if (seats < 2) {\n            revert E.InvalidSeats(seats);\n        }\n        if (cycles == 0) {\n            revert E.InvalidCycles(cycles);\n        }\n        if (creator == address(0)) {\n            revert E.InvalidCreator();\n        }\n        if ($.waitedFor != 0) {\n            revert E.GameAlreadyStarted();\n        }\n        $.roster = T.Roster({\n            creator: creator,\n            seats: seats,\n            started: false,\n            cycles: cycles,\n            startedWith: 0\n        });\n        if (options != bytes32(0)) {\n            $.gameOptions = options;\n        }\n        emit Ev.RosterOpened(creator, seats, cycles, options);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Seat a player who has just funded a reserve, if they need one.\n    /// @return waitNow Whether the cycle should wait for them from now on:\n    ///         always under open entry, only once started under a roster.\n    /// @dev UNDER A ROSTER NOBODY IS WAITED FOR UNTIL THE START, and that is\n    ///      what keeps the persistent world's commit and advance paths free of\n    ///      a roster read: a commitment before the start is refused because its\n    ///      player is not a member yet ({E-NotInGame}), and an advance because\n    ///      there is nobody to wait for ({E-NoOneToWaitFor}).\n    ///\n    ///      Anyone may fund anyone's reserve, so anyone may seat anyone. That\n    ///      is left open on purpose: it costs the giver a stake which the\n    ///      seated player may withdraw (freeing the seat before the start),\n    ///      and the acquisition rail stakes for a player from a contract.\n    function seat(uint256 player) internal returns (bool waitNow) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        T.Roster memory current = $.roster;\n        if (current.seats == 0) {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if ($.seatOf[player] == 0) {\n            if (current.started) {\n                revert E.GameAlreadyStarted();\n            }\n            uint256 seated = $.members.length;\n            if (seated >= current.seats) {\n                revert E.GameFull(current.seats);\n            }\n            $.members.push(player);\n            $.seatOf[player] = seated + 1;\n            emit Ev.SeatTaken(player, seated + 1);\n        }\n        return current.started;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Free a member's seat. Idempotent, and nothing under open entry.\n    /// @dev Before the start the seat can be taken again. After it, nobody\n    ///      joins, so a member who leaves (or is forfeited) is gone for good:\n    ///      D5's \"final, and final for free\".\n    function releaseSeat(uint256 player) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        uint256 indexPlusOne = $.seatOf[player];\n        if (indexPlusOne == 0) {\n            return;\n        }\n        uint256 last = $.members.length - 1;\n        if (indexPlusOne - 1 != last) {\n            uint256 moved = $.members[last];\n            $.members[indexPlusOne - 1] = moved;\n            $.seatOf[moved] = indexPlusOne;\n        }\n        $.members.pop();\n        $.seatOf[player] = 0;\n        emit Ev.SeatReleased(player, last);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Start a game with a closed roster: the members become who the\n    ///         cycle waits for, and the clock is re-anchored at this moment.\n    /// @param current Where the cycle is now, as the caller's `_cycle` reads it.\n    /// @param time The chain time, ignored under the manual policy.\n    /// @dev RE-ANCHORED AS AN EARLY CLOSE IS: the next cycle opens its commit\n    ///      phase now and runs its full length, so a game started near the end\n    ///      of the deployment's commit phase does not give its first turn a few\n    ///      seconds. It emits {Ev-CycleAdvanced} for the same reason an advance\n    ///      does: a reader folding the anchor needs no other event.\n    ///\n    ///      THE END IS FIXED HERE, as a cycle number: the roster's `cycles`\n    ///      counted from the first. Nothing runs when the game ends, since the\n    ///      clock is lazy; each action compares its cycle with this one.\n    function start(\n        Clock memory clock,\n        T.Cycle memory current,\n        uint256 time\n    ) internal returns (uint64 cycleNumber) {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        T.Roster memory opened = $.roster;\n        if (opened.seats == 0) {\n            revert E.NoRoster();\n        }\n        if (opened.started) {\n            revert E.GameAlreadyStarted();\n        }\n        uint256 seated = $.members.length;\n        if (seated < 2) {\n            revert E.NotEnoughMembers(seated);\n        }\n        $.roster.started = true;\n        $.roster.startedWith = uint8(seated);\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < seated; i++) {\n            startWaitingFor($.members[i]);\n        }\n\n        cycleNumber = current.cycleNumber + 1;\n        uint64 last = cycleNumber + opened.cycles - 1;\n        $.cycleState.lastCycleNumber = last;\n        $.cycleState.anchorCycleNumber = cycleNumber;\n        if (clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.Manual) {\n            $.cycleState.commiting = true;\n        } else {\n            $.cycleState.anchoredAt = uint64(time);\n        }\n\n        emit Ev.GameStarted(opened.creator, seated, last);\n        emit Ev.CycleAdvanced(cycleNumber, true, opened.creator);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The creator's forfeit of a member who has not acted: the cycle\n    ///         stops waiting for them, and their seat is gone.\n    /// @dev BOUNDED, SO THE POWER IS ONLY DECLARING THE OBVIOUS (D5): only in\n    ///      a commit phase, and only a member with no commitment in it. A\n    ///      member who has committed cannot be kicked; in a reveal phase the\n    ///      cycle waits for the commitments made, not for the members, so a\n    ///      forfeit there would unblock nothing and is refused. It settles\n    ///      nothing: a past commitment left open is settled as any missed\n    ///      reveal is, and the reserve stays its owner's to withdraw.\n    function forfeitMember(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint64 cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting\n    ) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        T.Roster memory current = $.roster;\n        if (current.seats == 0) {\n            revert E.NoRoster();\n        }\n        if (!current.started) {\n            revert E.GameNotStarted();\n        }\n        if ($.seatOf[player] == 0) {\n            revert E.NotInGame(player);\n        }\n        // After the end nothing is unblocked by it, and a member forfeited\n        // then would only be one fewer member when the game counts who played.\n        if (isPastTheEnd(cycleNumber)) {\n            revert E.GameEnded($.cycleState.lastCycleNumber);\n        }\n        if (!commiting) {\n            revert E.InRevealPhase(cycleNumber);\n        }\n        if ($.commitments[player].cycleNumber == cycleNumber) {\n            revert E.MemberHasActed(player, cycleNumber);\n        }\n        releaseSeat(player);\n        stopWaitingFor(player);\n        emit Ev.MemberForfeited(player, cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // COMMIT\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function commitmentOf(\n        uint256 player\n    ) internal view returns (T.Commitment memory) {\n        return layout().commitments[player];\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Bond part of a reserve to the head of a turn's hash chain.\n    /// @dev ONLY A MEMBER MAY TAKE A TURN, and the reason is arithmetic rather\n    ///      than etiquette: unanimity compares how many have committed against\n    ///      how many the cycle waits for, and those two have to count the SAME\n    ///      SET or the comparison means nothing. Without this any address at\n    ///      all could commit - a bond of zero against a reserve of zero passes\n    ///      every other check here - and enough throwaway addresses could close\n    ///      the commit phase before a real player had acted.\n    ///\n    ///      Counted once per player per cycle, not once per call: replacing a\n    ///      commitment made this cycle is allowed, and counting it again would\n    ///      let one player alone satisfy unanimity for the whole set.\n    function commit(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond,\n        uint64 cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting\n    ) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        // The slot the cycle was read from, so this costs a warm read; first,\n        // so that after the end every commitment is told the game has ended.\n        uint64 last = $.cycleState.lastCycleNumber;\n        if (last != 0 && cycleNumber > last) {\n            revert E.GameEnded(last);\n        }\n        if (!commiting) {\n            revert E.InRevealPhase(cycleNumber);\n        }\n        if (!$.isWaitedFor[player]) {\n            revert E.NotInGame(player);\n        }\n\n        uint256 reserve = $.reserve[player];\n        if (bond > reserve) {\n            revert E.ReserveTooLow(reserve, bond);\n        }\n\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = $.commitments[player];\n        if (\n            commitment.cycleNumber != 0 && commitment.cycleNumber != cycleNumber\n        ) {\n            revert E.PreviousCommitmentNotRevealed();\n        }\n\n        if (commitment.cycleNumber != cycleNumber) {\n            _recordCommitment($, cycleNumber);\n        }\n\n        commitment.hash = commitmentHash;\n        commitment.cycleNumber = cycleNumber;\n        commitment.bond = bond;\n\n        emit Ev.CommitmentMade(player, cycleNumber, commitmentHash, bond);\n    }\n\n    function cancel(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint64 cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting\n    ) internal {\n        if (!commiting) {\n            revert E.InRevealPhase(cycleNumber);\n        }\n\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = $.commitments[player];\n        if (commitment.cycleNumber == 0) {\n            revert E.NoCommitmentToCancel();\n        }\n        if (commitment.cycleNumber != cycleNumber) {\n            revert E.PreviousCommitmentNotRevealed();\n        }\n\n        // The hash is not reset, so the slot is never zeroed and the gas cost\n        // of the next commitment stays the same whatever happened before it.\n        commitment.cycleNumber = 0;\n        T.CycleTally storage tally = $.tally;\n        if (tally.cycleNumber == cycleNumber && tally.committed != 0) {\n            tally.committed -= 1;\n        }\n\n        emit Ev.CommitmentCancelled(player, cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // REVEAL\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Check a chunk revealed in its own cycle. Writes nothing.\n    function openChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint64 cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 actionsPerReveal\n    ) internal view returns (Chunk memory chunk) {\n        if (commiting) {\n            revert E.InCommitmentPhase(cycleNumber);\n        }\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = layout().commitments[player];\n        uint64 committedIn = commitment.cycleNumber;\n        if (committedIn == 0) {\n            revert E.NothingToReveal();\n        }\n        if (committedIn != cycleNumber) {\n            revert E.InvalidCycle(cycleNumber, committedIn);\n        }\n        bytes24 head = commitment.hash;\n        _checkChunk(head, digest, numActions, furtherActions, actionsPerReveal);\n        chunk = Chunk({\n            player: player,\n            cycleNumber: cycleNumber,\n            commitmentHash: head,\n            furtherActions: furtherActions,\n            missed: false\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Apply what an opened chunk cost, and move the chain on.\n    /// @dev THE COST IS TAKEN FROM THE BOND AND FROM THE RESERVE, and a chunk\n    ///      that costs more than the bond still holds is refused: the bond was\n    ///      fixed before anybody could see the board this resolution ran\n    ///      against, so it is the most a turn can spend.\n    ///\n    ///      THE CYCLE'S TALLY COUNTS TURNS, NOT TRANSACTIONS. The reveal is\n    ///      recorded only on the chunk that closes the chain: counting a\n    ///      partial reveal would let unanimity close the cycle while a player\n    ///      still had chunks owed, and those chunks would then be unrevealable.\n    ///\n    ///      The surplus of a bond that exceeded the turn goes back to being\n    ///      ordinary reserve when the last chunk lands.\n    function closeRevealedChunk(Chunk memory chunk, uint256 cost) internal {\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = $.commitments[chunk.player];\n        uint256 bond = commitment.bond;\n        if (cost > bond) {\n            revert E.BondTooLow(bond, cost);\n        }\n        if (cost != 0) {\n            $.reserve[chunk.player] -= cost;\n            commitment.bond = bond - cost;\n        }\n\n        if (chunk.furtherActions != bytes24(0)) {\n            commitment.hash = chunk.furtherActions;\n        } else {\n            commitment.cycleNumber = 0;\n            commitment.bond = 0;\n            T.CycleTally storage tally = $.tally;\n            if (tally.cycleNumber == chunk.cycleNumber) {\n                tally.revealed += 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        emit Ev.CommitmentRevealed(\n            chunk.player,\n            chunk.cycleNumber,\n            chunk.commitmentHash,\n            chunk.furtherActions,\n            cost\n        );\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // SETTLING A MISSED REVEAL\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Check a chunk of a commitment whose cycle is over. Writes\n    ///         nothing.\n    /// @dev The same chain and the same length rules as a reveal, so the\n    ///      settlement is shown exactly what a reveal would have been shown.\n    function openMissedChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint64 cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 actionsPerReveal\n    ) internal view returns (Chunk memory chunk) {\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = layout().commitments[player];\n        uint64 committedIn = commitment.cycleNumber;\n        if (committedIn == 0) {\n            revert E.NothingToReveal();\n        }\n        if (committedIn == cycleNumber) {\n            revert E.CanStillReveal(cycleNumber);\n        }\n        bytes24 head = commitment.hash;\n        _checkChunk(head, digest, numActions, furtherActions, actionsPerReveal);\n        chunk = Chunk({\n            player: player,\n            cycleNumber: cycleNumber,\n            commitmentHash: head,\n            furtherActions: furtherActions,\n            missed: true\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Earmark the penalty for an opened missed chunk, and move the\n    ///         chain on.\n    /// @return charged How much of the bond the penalty takes: the penalty,\n    ///         capped at what the bond still holds. Forfeiting it is the\n    ///         caller's, through its `_forfeit` seam.\n    /// @dev On the last chunk the commitment closes and whatever is left of\n    ///      the bond is reserve again: what was committed has been established\n    ///      and paid for, so the rest was only ever hiding the turn's length.\n    function closeMissedChunk(\n        Chunk memory chunk,\n        uint256 penalty\n    ) internal returns (uint256 charged) {\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = layout().commitments[chunk.player];\n        uint256 bond = commitment.bond;\n        charged = penalty > bond ? bond : penalty;\n        if (chunk.furtherActions != bytes24(0)) {\n            commitment.bond = bond - charged;\n            commitment.hash = chunk.furtherActions;\n        } else {\n            commitment.cycleNumber = 0;\n            commitment.bond = 0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Close a missed commitment without being shown its chunks.\n    /// @return head The head it was holding.\n    /// @return bond What was still bonded, all of which the caller forfeits.\n    function voidCommitment(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal returns (bytes24 head, uint256 bond) {\n        T.Commitment storage commitment = layout().commitments[player];\n        uint64 committedIn = commitment.cycleNumber;\n        if (committedIn == 0) {\n            revert E.NothingToReveal();\n        }\n        if (committedIn == cycleNumber) {\n            revert E.CanStillReveal(cycleNumber);\n        }\n        head = commitment.hash;\n        bond = commitment.bond;\n        commitment.cycleNumber = 0;\n        commitment.bond = 0;\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // THE CYCLE\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice WHERE THE CYCLE IS, under any of the three policies.\n    /// @param time The chain time, ignored under the manual policy.\n    /// @dev ONE PIECE OF ARITHMETIC SERVES ALL THREE TIMED READINGS, because\n    ///      they differ only in where the anchor is. The anchor is the start of\n    ///      a cycle's COMMIT phase: for `Timed` it never moves from (cycle 2,\n    ///      startTime); for `TimedWithEarlyAdvance` an early advance moves it\n    ///      to the moment of the advance, and the clock carries on from there.\n    ///      `Manual` has no clock at all, so the stored state IS the answer.\n    ///\n    ///      Cycles start at 2 so that the hypothetical reveal phase before the\n    ///      first commit phase can be cycle 1, which is also why zero can mean\n    ///      \"no commitment\" in {UsingCommitRevealTypes-Commitment}.\n    function cycle(\n        Clock memory clock,\n        uint256 time\n    ) internal view returns (T.Cycle memory result) {\n        T.CycleState memory state = layout().cycleState;\n        bool anchored = state.anchorCycleNumber != 0;\n        uint64 anchorCycleNumber = anchored ? state.anchorCycleNumber : 2;\n\n        if (clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.Manual) {\n            // No clock, so no phase bounds: zero here means \"there is nothing\n            // to count down to\".\n            return\n                T.Cycle({\n                    cycleNumber: anchorCycleNumber,\n                    commiting: anchored ? state.commiting : true,\n                    phaseStart: 0,\n                    phaseEnd: 0\n                });\n        }\n\n        uint256 anchoredAt = anchored ? state.anchoredAt : clock.startTime;\n        if (time < anchoredAt) {\n            revert E.GameNotStarted();\n        }\n\n        uint256 cycleDuration =\n            clock.commitPhaseDuration + clock.revealPhaseDuration;\n        uint256 elapsed = time - anchoredAt;\n        result.cycleNumber =\n            anchorCycleNumber + uint64(elapsed / cycleDuration);\n        result.commiting =\n            (elapsed % cycleDuration) < clock.commitPhaseDuration;\n\n        uint256 cycleStart =\n            anchoredAt +\n                uint256(result.cycleNumber - anchorCycleNumber) * cycleDuration;\n\n        // AN EARLY OPEN MOVES THE START AND NOT THE DEADLINE. The reveal window\n        // becomes \"as soon as everyone has committed, until the nominal end\",\n        // which is strictly wider than the window the clock alone would have\n        // given: a reveal scheduled against the nominal time still lands inside\n        // it. Shifting the deadline forward instead would lose exactly those\n        // reveals, and lose them silently, at the cost of the stake.\n        bool openedEarly =\n            clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.TimedWithEarlyAdvance &&\n                state.earlyRevealCycleNumber == result.cycleNumber;\n        if (openedEarly) {\n            result.commiting = false;\n        }\n\n        if (result.commiting) {\n            result.phaseStart = uint64(cycleStart);\n            result.phaseEnd = uint64(cycleStart + clock.commitPhaseDuration);\n        } else {\n            result.phaseStart =\n                openedEarly\n                    ? state.earlyRevealAt\n                    : uint64(cycleStart + clock.commitPhaseDuration);\n            result.phaseEnd = uint64(cycleStart + cycleDuration);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Move the cycle on, if the rules already permit it.\n    /// @param current Where the cycle is now, as the caller's `_cycle` seam\n    ///        reads it.\n    /// @param time The chain time, ignored under the manual policy.\n    /// @dev UNANIMITY, NEVER A MAJORITY OR A QUORUM. If a subset could close a\n    ///      phase, fast players would time out slow ones and the cycle would\n    ///      become a race. And IT ONLY EVER WIDENS A WINDOW: opening the reveal\n    ///      phase early does not move its deadline, and closing the cycle early\n    ///      is only permitted once every commitment in it has been revealed,\n    ///      so there is no window left to shorten.
