Evaluated at execution\n    ///      time, which is what makes it airtight: a reveal still in the\n    ///      mempool has not been counted, so an advance mined before it\n    ///      reverts rather than stranding it.\n    function advance(\n        Clock memory clock,\n        T.Cycle memory current,\n        uint256 time\n    ) internal returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) {\n        if (clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.Timed) {\n            // The cycle simply IS what the clock says, so there is nothing\n            // here for anyone to do.\n            revert E.NextPhaseNotAllowed();\n        }\n\n        Layout storage $ = layout();\n        // AFTER THE LAST CYCLE NOTHING MOVES. Closing the last cycle early, once\n        // all its reveals are in, is not refused: it ends the game sooner, and\n        // a later reader sees the same end either way.\n        if (isPastTheEnd(current.cycleNumber)) {\n            revert E.GameEnded($.cycleState.lastCycleNumber);\n        }\n        T.Attendance memory present = attendance(current.cycleNumber);\n\n        // No closed set, no denominator. Without this one caller could push an\n        // empty game forward as fast as they liked.\n        if (present.waitedFor == 0) {\n            revert E.NoOneToWaitFor();\n        }\n\n        if (current.commiting) {\n            if (present.committed < present.waitedFor) {\n                revert E.StillWaitingToCommit(\n                    present.committed,\n                    present.waitedFor\n                );\n            }\n            cycleNumber = current.cycleNumber;\n            commiting = false;\n\n            if (clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.Manual) {\n                $.cycleState.anchorCycleNumber = cycleNumber;\n                $.cycleState.commiting = false;\n            } else {\n                // The reveal window opens NOW and closes when it always would\n                // have. Recording only that it opened early is what keeps the\n                // deadline where it was.\n                $.cycleState.earlyRevealCycleNumber = cycleNumber;\n                $.cycleState.earlyRevealAt = uint64(time);\n            }\n        } else {\n            if (present.revealed < present.committed) {\n                revert E.StillWaitingToReveal(\n                    present.revealed,\n                    present.committed\n                );\n            }\n            cycleNumber = current.cycleNumber + 1;\n            commiting = true;\n\n            $.cycleState.anchorCycleNumber = cycleNumber;\n            if (clock.policy == T.CyclePolicy.Manual) {\n                $.cycleState.commiting = true;\n            } else {\n                // The new cycle runs its full length from here, which is the\n                // only way early advance makes a game with a clock finish a\n                // cycle sooner than the clock would.\n                $.cycleState.anchoredAt = uint64(time);\n            }\n        }\n\n        emit Ev.CycleAdvanced(cycleNumber, commiting, msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // INTERNALS\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @dev TWO LENGTH RULES, AND NEITHER IS TIDINESS. A chunk may never carry\n    ///      more than the configured number, or the bound the whole design\n    ///      exists for would hold for every reveal except the last of each\n    ///      turn. And a chunk that promises a successor must be exactly FULL,\n    ///      or a player dribbles one action per transaction and spreads a turn\n    ///      across unbounded reveals.\n    function _checkChunk(\n        bytes24 head,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 actionsPerReveal\n    ) private pure {\n        if (numActions > actionsPerReveal) {\n            revert E.TooManyActions(numActions, actionsPerReveal);\n        }\n        if (furtherActions != bytes24(0) && numActions != actionsPerReveal) {\n            revert E.InvalidFurtherActions(numActions, actionsPerReveal);\n        }\n        if (head != digest) {\n            revert E.CommitmentHashNotMatching();\n        }\n    }\n\n    function _recordCommitment(Layout storage $, uint64 cycleNumber) private {\n        T.CycleTally storage tally = $.tally;\n        if (tally.cycleNumber != cycleNumber) {\n            $.tally = T.CycleTally({\n                cycleNumber: cycleNumber,\n                committed: 1,\n                revealed: 0\n            });\n        } else {\n            tally.committed += 1;\n        }\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xeaa3e772b7149a09820286748c5b1c232d472eb1cb1f679cc3a876b7a6dfca16","license":"AGPL-3.0"},"project/src/commit-reveal/UsingCommitReveal.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {ITime} from \"solidity-kit/solc_0_8/debug/time/interfaces/ITime.sol\";\nimport {Delegation} from \"@etherplay/delegation/contracts/Delegation.sol\";\nimport {UsingCommitRevealEvents} from \"./interfaces/UsingCommitRevealEvents.sol\";\nimport {UsingCommitRevealErrors} from \"./interfaces/UsingCommitRevealErrors.sol\";\nimport {CommitReveal} from \"./CommitReveal.sol\";\n\n/// @title UsingCommitReveal\n/// @notice The {CommitReveal} library, wired to its configuration and to the\n///         three seams a game varies at. What a game inherits to be a\n///         commit-reveal game, and the reason it does not write one.\n///\n/// THE CONFIGURATION IS IMMUTABLE, so the hot path reads no storage for it:\n/// the chunk size, the phase durations and the policy are compiled into each\n/// route's bytecode by its constructor. Every route behind a router is built\n/// with the same config, which is what the deploy script is for.\n///\n/// THREE SEAMS, AND NOTHING ELSE HERE IS VIRTUAL. {_playerOf} decides who the\n/// caller acts for (an account through delegation by default, a token in a\n/// custody game). {_forfeit} decides what a missed reveal costs (the bond out\n/// of the reserve by default, custody of a token elsewhere). {_cycle} decides\n/// where the cycle is (the three policies by default). A game overrides one\n/// function per axis and touches no store and no other internal.\n///\n/// A GAME'S ACTIONS NEVER COME IN. A game keeps its own typed routes, hashes\n/// its own action type in the one encoding\n/// `bytes24(keccak256(abi.encode(secret, actions, furtherActions)))`, and\n/// calls {_openChunk} with the digest and the count, resolves its actions,\n/// then calls {_closeChunk} with what they cost. The settlement of a missed\n/// reveal shown the chunks is the same pair, opened with {_openMissedChunk}\n/// and closed with the game's penalty.\nabstract contract UsingCommitReveal is\n    UsingCommitRevealEvents,\n    UsingCommitRevealErrors\n{\n    /// @notice the timestamp (in seconds) at which the game starts, in its\n    ///         commit phase\n    uint256 internal immutable START_TIME;\n    /// @notice the duration of the commit phase in seconds\n    uint256 internal immutable COMMIT_PHASE_DURATION;\n    /// @notice the duration of the reveal phase in seconds\n    uint256 internal immutable REVEAL_PHASE_DURATION;\n    /// @notice a time source for tests and local play, or zero for the chain's\n    ITime internal immutable TIME;\n    /// @notice THE CHUNK: how many actions one reveal transaction may carry.\n    /// @dev It bounds the TRANSACTION and not the TURN. A turn arrives in as\n    ///      many reveals as it takes; a cap on how many actions a turn may\n    ///      contain is a game RULE, and the base takes no position on it.\n    uint256 internal immutable ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL;\n    /// @notice how the cycle advances: see {UsingCommitRevealTypes-CyclePolicy}\n    CyclePolicy internal immutable CYCLE_POLICY;\n\n    constructor(CommitRevealConfig memory config) {\n        // THE ARITHMETIC THE WHOLE CYCLE RESTS ON, checked once here rather\n        // than trusted forever. A cycle is a commit phase followed by a reveal\n        // phase and nothing else, so a commitment made in the CURRENT cycle is\n        // always still openable. A zero phase punches a hole straight through\n        // that - a zero reveal phase makes every commitment unopenable and a\n        // zero commit phase makes every commitment impossible - and the hole\n        // is silent, because it costs the first player their stake rather than\n        // reverting anything. A manual game has no clock, so durations there\n        // would describe a schedule that does not exist: refused too.\n        if (config.cyclePolicy == CyclePolicy.Manual) {\n            if (\n                config.commitPhaseDuration != 0 ||\n                config.revealPhaseDuration != 0\n            ) {\n                revert InvalidCycleConfiguration();\n            }\n        } else if (\n            config.commitPhaseDuration == 0 || config.revealPhaseDuration == 0\n        ) {\n            revert InvalidCycleConfiguration();\n        }\n\n        // THE SAME CLASS OF HOLE, one level down. A chunk of zero actions makes\n        // every reveal revert, so every turn is committed and none can ever be\n        // opened, and the bond is taken by the settlement.\n        if (config.actionsPerReveal == 0) {\n            revert InvalidActionsPerReveal();\n        }\n\n        START_TIME = config.startTime;\n        COMMIT_PHASE_DURATION = config.commitPhaseDuration;\n        REVEAL_PHASE_DURATION = config.revealPhaseDuration;\n        TIME = config.time;\n        ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL = config.actionsPerReveal;\n        CYCLE_POLICY = config.cyclePolicy;\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // RESERVE\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _reserveOf(uint256 player) internal view returns (uint256) {\n        return CommitReveal.reserveOf(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Credit a reserve, and make its holder a member.\n    /// @dev WHAT MAKES SOMEONE A MEMBER IS THE GAME'S ANSWER, and a reserve\n    ///      game's is a funded reserve: holding one is exactly what lets an\n    ///      account play, so it is what the cycle waits for. A game whose\n    ///      entry is custody of a token calls {_takeSeat} from wherever\n    ///      custody is taken instead, and never funds a reserve.\n    ///\n    ///      UNDER A CLOSED ROSTER a funded reserve is a SEAT ({_openRoster}):\n    ///      refused once the game has started or when every seat is taken,\n    ///      and waited for only from the start.\n    function _addToReserve(uint256 player, uint256 amount) internal {\n        uint256 newAmount = CommitReveal.deposit(player, amount);\n        if (newAmount != 0) {\n            _takeSeat(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Debit a reserve on its owner's request; emptying it is leaving.\n    /// @dev Leaving settles nothing and costs nothing beyond the departure:\n    ///      leaving the set the cycle waits for and being punished for going\n    ///      silent are different questions, and only the first is the cycle's.\n    function _withdrawFromReserve(uint256 player, uint256 amount) internal {\n        uint256 newAmount = CommitReveal.withdraw(player, amount);\n        if (newAmount == 0) {\n            _leaveSeat(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // A CLOSED ROSTER\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Make this a game for a fixed set of members: `seats` of them,\n    ///         seated by funding a reserve, started by `creator`, ending\n    ///         `cycles` cycles after its start, with `options` for the game.\n    /// @dev OPT-IN, AND ONCE. A game that never calls this (the persistent\n    ///      world) has open entry, exactly as before rosters existed. A game\n    ///      cloned per table calls it from its initialiser, in the same\n    ///      transaction as the clone is made, so nobody can open it first.\n    ///\n    ///      The roster's rules, in one place: a seat is taken by funding a\n    ///      reserve while the game has not started and a seat is free; a\n    ///      seated member may top up at any time; emptying a reserve is\n    ///      leaving (before the start the seat can be taken again, after it\n    ///      nobody joins); the creator starts the game once two are seated\n    ///      ({_startGame}), and may forfeit a member who has not acted\n    ///      ({_forfeitMember}); after its last cycle nobody commits, advances\n    ///      or is forfeited ({_hasEnded}), while that cycle's reveals and every\n    ///      missed reveal's settlement still go through.\n    function _openRoster(\n        address creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 options\n    ) internal {\n        CommitReveal.openRoster(creator, seats, cycles, options);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Seat a player, and wait for them if the game has started (or\n    ///         has open entry). What a custody game calls where it takes\n    ///         custody, in place of {_startWaitingFor}.\n    function _takeSeat(uint256 player) internal {\n        if (CommitReveal.seat(player)) {\n            CommitReveal.startWaitingFor(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Leave: stop waiting for this player and free their seat.\n    function _leaveSeat(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.releaseSeat(player);\n        CommitReveal.stopWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Start a game with a closed roster.\n    /// @param sender Who is starting it, normally `msg.sender`: the creator,\n    ///        or a delegate of theirs (their browser's key).\n    function _startGame(address sender) internal returns (uint64 cycleNumber) {\n        Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, _requireRosterCreator());\n        return\n            CommitReveal.start(\n                _clock(),\n                _cycle(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The creator's forfeit of a member who has not acted in the\n    ///         current phase. See {CommitReveal-forfeitMember}.\n    /// @param sender Who is forfeiting, normally `msg.sender`: the creator,\n    ///        or a delegate of theirs.\n    function _forfeitMember(address sender, uint256 player) internal {\n        Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, _requireRosterCreator());\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.forfeitMember(player, cycleNumber, commiting);\n    }\n\n    function _roster() internal view returns (Roster memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.roster();\n    }\n\n    function _members() internal view returns (uint256[] memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.members();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHAT THE GAME READS AT THIS TABLE, as its creator chose it.\n    /// @dev Opaque to the base, and the only way a game's routes learn\n    ///      anything chosen at creation: each route is its own contract\n    ///      behind the router, so the lobby's route cannot call a game's hook.\n    ///      A game decodes it in its own routes (and refuses what it cannot\n    ///      read); zero under open entry, and wherever the creator sent none.\n    function _gameOptions() internal view returns (bytes32) {\n        return CommitReveal.gameOptions();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice THE END'S HOOK: the last cycle this game plays, or zero if it\n    ///         has none (open entry, or a roster not started yet).\n    function _lastCycleNumber() internal view returns (uint64) {\n        return CommitReveal.lastCycleNumber();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice THE END'S HOOK: whether the game has played its last cycle.\n    /// @dev A comparison, never an event: nothing runs at the moment a game\n    ///      ends, so a game's own routes (a settlement, a score) ask this.\n    function _hasEnded() internal view returns (bool) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return CommitReveal.isPastTheEnd(cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The creator, or a revert: under open entry there is nobody to\n    ///      ask, and `Delegation` would read a zero creator as \"the sender\".\n    function _requireRosterCreator() private view returns (address) {\n        Roster memory opened = CommitReveal.roster();\n        if (opened.seats == 0) {\n            revert NoRoster();\n        }\n        return opened.creator;\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // WHO THE CYCLE WAITS FOR\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Start blocking the cycle on this player. Idempotent.\n    function _startWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.startWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Stop blocking the cycle on this player. Idempotent.\n    function _stopWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.stopWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    function _isWaitedFor(uint256 player) internal view returns (bool) {\n        return CommitReveal.isWaitedFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The denominator, and how much of it has acted this cycle.\n    function _attendance(\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (Attendance memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.attendance(cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // COMMIT / REVEAL\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _commitmentOf(\n        uint256 player\n    ) internal view returns (Commitment memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.commitmentOf(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Bond part of a reserve to a turn this cycle. `player` must\n    ///         already be resolved by {_playerOf}.\n    function _makeCommitment(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond\n    ) internal {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.commit(\n            player,\n            commitmentHash,\n            bond,\n            cycleNumber,\n            commiting\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Take a commitment back while its commit phase is still open.\n    ///         `player` must already be resolved by {_playerOf}.\n    function _cancelCommitment(uint256 player) internal {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.cancel(player, cycleNumber, commiting);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Check one chunk of a reveal, before the game resolves it.\n    /// @param digest The game's hash of the chunk, in the one encoding:\n    ///        `bytes24(keccak256(abi.encode(secret, actions, furtherActions)))`.\n    /// @param numActions How many actions the chunk carries.\n    /// @param furtherActions The hash of the next chunk, or zero for the last.\n    /// @return chunk What {_closeChunk} needs once the game has resolved it.\n    /// @dev ANYONE MAY REVEAL, which is why this takes no sender: a reveal is\n    ///      validated by the hash, and accepting it from anyone is what stops\n    ///      an offline player forfeiting.\n    ///\n    ///      ORDER INDEPENDENCE IS THE GAME'S TO KEEP between this call and the\n    ///      next. Reveals arrive in whatever order the mempool delivers them,\n    ///      and the board after a cycle must not depend on that: accumulate,\n    ///      never branch on what another reveal of the same cycle could have\n    ///      changed. See `AGENTS.md`, \"Commit-reveal rules\".\n    function _openChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal view returns (CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        return\n            CommitReveal.openChunk(\n                player,\n                cycleNumber,\n                commiting,\n                digest,\n                numActions,\n                furtherActions,\n                ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Check one chunk of a MISSED reveal: a commitment whose cycle is\n    ///         over, settled by being shown what it committed to.\n    /// @dev ANYONE MAY SETTLE THIS WAY, because nothing in it can hurt the\n    ///      player more than their own silence already has: the chain checks\n    ///      that the chunks are exactly what was committed, the game takes its\n    ///      penalty for exactly those actions, and the surplus of the bond goes\n    ///      back to the player. Nobody but the player receives anything, so a\n    ///      stranger settling gains nothing either, which is what makes it safe\n    ///      to leave open. Who can is whoever holds the chunks: the player's\n    ///      own client, a reveal service, a world playing its own seats.\n    ///\n    ///      Why it exists at all: a bond may exceed what the turn costs, since a\n    ///      bond equal to the exact cost tells everyone how many actions the\n    ///      commitment hides. Without the chunks the contract cannot tell the\n    ///      surplus from the stake, so forfeiting all of it would punish the\n    ///      hiding rather than the silence. See {_forfeitMissedReveal} for the\n    ///      settlement that is not shown the chunks.\n    function _openMissedChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal view returns (CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return\n            CommitReveal.openMissedChunk(\n                player,\n                cycleNumber,\n                digest,\n                numActions,\n                furtherActions,\n                ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Apply an opened chunk: charge its cost (a reveal) or forfeit\n    ///         its penalty (a missed reveal), and move the chain on.\n    /// @param amount For a reveal, what the game's resolution reports the\n    ///        chunk cost, taken from the bond and the reserve; a chunk costing\n    ///        more than the bond still holds is refused. For a missed reveal,\n    ///        the game's penalty for the chunk's actions, capped at the bond\n    ///        and handed to {_forfeit}.\n    /// @return taken What was charged, or what {_forfeit} took.\n    function _closeChunk(\n        CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (uint256 taken) {\n        if (!chunk.missed) {\n            CommitReveal.closeRevealedChunk(chunk, amount);\n            return amount;\n        }\n        uint256 charged = CommitReveal.closeMissedChunk(chunk, amount);\n        taken = _forfeit(chunk.player, charged);\n        emit CommitmentVoid(\n            chunk.player,\n            chunk.cycleNumber,\n            chunk.commitmentHash,\n            chunk.furtherActions,\n            taken\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Settle a missed reveal WITHOUT its chunks: the whole remaining\n    ///         bond is forfeited.\n    /// @param sender Who is settling, normally `msg.sender`.\n    /// @param id The identity, as the client named it.\n    /// @dev ONLY THE PLAYER OR THEIR DELEGATE, resolved here through\n    ///      {_playerOf} so that no route can skip it. A stranger could\n    ///      otherwise take a bond whose surplus the player could have\n    ///      recovered by settling with the chunks. A player who has lost their\n    ///      plan, or who simply wants to play again, still has this route, and\n    ///      it is always available: it needs nothing but the identity.\n    ///\n    ///      LIVENESS IS UNCHANGED BY IT. A member whose past commitment nobody\n    ///      settles cannot commit, so the cycle waits for them exactly as for a\n    ///      member who does not commit: under a timed policy the clock moves on\n    ///      and only early advance is lost.\n    function _forfeitMissedReveal(address sender, uint256 id) internal {\n        uint256 player = _playerOf(sender, id);\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        (bytes24 head, uint256 bond) = CommitReveal.voidCommitment(\n            player,\n            cycleNumber\n        );\n        uint256 forfeited = _forfeit(player, bond);\n        emit CommitmentVoid(player, cycleNumber, head, bytes24(0), forfeited);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // ADVANCING THE CYCLE\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Move the cycle on, if the rules already permit it.\n    /// @dev ITS OWN TRANSACTION, NEVER A RIDER ON THE LAST REVEAL: advancing\n    ///      inside a reveal would make that call mean something different\n    ///      depending on whether you happened to be last, would make its gas\n    ///      depend on winning a race, and would not be retriable. Permissionless\n    ///      but strictly conditional, so letting anyone call it grants nothing.\n    ///      See {CommitReveal-advance} for unanimity and for why it only ever\n    ///      widens a window.\n    function _advanceCycle()\n        internal\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting)\n    {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.advance(\n                _clock(),\n                _cycle(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // THE SEAMS\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice WHO THE CALLER IS ACTING FOR, having checked that they may.\n    /// @param sender The account or key that sent the transaction.\n    /// @param id The identity, as the client named it.\n    /// @return player The identity this action is filed under, which is what\n    ///         every record in {CommitReveal} is keyed by.\n    /// @dev THE DEFAULT IS AN ADDRESS GAME: the identity is the account, and\n    ///      the only question is authority, answered by the delegation\n    ///      library, so a local signer may act for the account that authorised\n    ///      it. A token game overrides this to resolve a token and check that\n    ///      the caller may act for its owner. RESOLUTION AND AUTHORITY ARE ONE\n    ///      FUNCTION ON PURPOSE: splitting them would let a caller reach a\n    ///      resolved identity without having passed the check.\n    function _playerOf(\n        address sender,\n        uint256 id\n    ) internal view virtual returns (uint256 player) {\n        // An identity that is not an address CANNOT BE ONE HERE: two ids that\n        // differ above the 160th bit would otherwise be the same player,\n        // sharing one reserve and one commitment, with nothing raised anywhere.\n        if (id > type(uint160).max) {\n            revert InvalidPlayer(id);\n        }\n        // Zero means \"whoever is calling\", which the library resolves.\n        return\n            uint256(\n                uint160(\n                    Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, address(uint160(id)))\n                )\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHAT NOT REVEALING COSTS.\n    /// @param amount What the settlement says is at stake: the game's penalty\n    ///        for the chunks it was shown, or the whole remaining bond when it\n    ///        was shown none.\n    /// @return forfeited How much of it was taken, for the event.\n    /// @dev The framework's only requirement is that SOMETHING is lost: a\n    ///      player who dislikes what they committed to can always go quiet.\n    ///      The default takes the amount out of the reserve and leaves it in\n    ///      the contract. A game whose stake is custody of a token seizes the\n    ///      token here instead and returns zero - on BOTH settlement routes,\n    ///      since a custody game bonds nothing and \"only the penalty for what\n    ///      was committed\" would otherwise cost a player nothing.\n    ///\n    ///      NOTHING FORFEITED GOES TO WHOEVER SETTLED. A settler that could\n    ///      profit would race the player for their own surplus.\n    function _forfeit(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal virtual returns (uint256 forfeited) {\n        return CommitReveal.debit(player, amount);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHERE THE CYCLE IS. The seam the cycle policy varies at.\n    /// @dev The only thing about the clock that is virtual: a game with a\n    ///      fourth policy overrides this one function. {_cycleNumber} is\n    ///      derived from it rather than the other way round.\n    function _cycle() internal view virtual returns (Cycle memory) {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.cycle(\n                _clock(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The cycle as everything inside this contract asks about it.\n    /// @dev Deliberately NOT virtual: {_cycle} is the seam.\n    function _cycleNumber()\n        internal\n        view\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting)\n    {\n        Cycle memory current = _cycle();\n        return (current.cycleNumber, current.commiting);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // INTERNALS\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _clock() internal view returns (CommitReveal.Clock memory) {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.Clock({\n                policy: CYCLE_POLICY,\n                startTime: START_TIME,\n                commitPhaseDuration: COMMIT_PHASE_DURATION,\n                revealPhaseDuration: REVEAL_PHASE_DURATION\n            });\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The chain's time, or a test's.\n    function _timestamp() internal view returns (uint256) {\n        if (address(TIME) == address(0)) {\n            return block.timestamp;\n        }\n        return TIME.timestamp();\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x51a932e6e94dbb958d7a74bd7197cfe428e314755bb8e50128d5175b269b9982","license":"AGPL-3.0"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/ICommitRevealLobby.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealTypes} from \"./UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol\";\n\n/// @title What a game for a fixed set of members exposes\n/// @notice The routes a game adds to be cloned per table by\n///         {CommitRevealGameFactory}: the initialiser the factory calls, the\n///         creator's two powers, and the roster as a client reads it. The rules\n///         are the base's ({UsingCommitReveal-_openRoster}); a game's route only\n///         forwards to them.\ninterface ICommitRevealLobby is UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice Give this game a closed roster of `seats`, created by `creator`,\n    ///         playing `cycles` cycles from its start, with the game's own\n    ///         `gameOptions` (opaque to the base; zero for none).\n    /// @dev Once. The factory calls it in the transaction that makes the\n    ///      clone, so nobody can open a clone's roster before it does.\n    function initializeLobby(\n        address creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 gameOptions\n    ) external;\n\n    /// @notice Start the game: the creator (or a delegate of theirs), once two\n    ///         or more are seated. Closes the roster and re-anchors the clock.\n    function start() external returns (uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice Forfeit a member who has not committed in the current commit\n    ///         phase: the creator (or a delegate of theirs) only.\n    function forfeitMember(uint256 player) external;\n\n    /// @notice The roster, and who holds a seat.\n    function getRoster()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (Roster memory roster, uint256[] memory members);\n\n    /// @notice Where the game is against its end: the current cycle, the last\n    ///         it plays (zero before the start), and whether it is past it.\n    function getEnd()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, uint64 lastCycleNumber, bool ended);\n\n    /// @notice Whether the game has played its last cycle.\n    function hasEnded() external view returns (bool);\n\n    /// @notice What the game's own rules read at this table, as created.\n    function getGameOptions() external view returns (bytes32);\n}\n","keccak256":"0xf0cf4c2589e71826b360f5c82c697ef7a2952352d6f489f78db782cc3e1d27ee","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealErrors.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\n/// @title The errors of the commit-reveal base\n/// @dev Raised by {CommitReveal} and {UsingCommitReveal} through qualified\n///      names, and inherited by a game's own errors interface so that they are\n///      in the game's ABI where a client decodes them.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealErrors {\n    /// @notice the game has not started yet\n    error GameNotStarted();\n\n    /// @notice trying to commit while the reveal phase is running\n    error InRevealPhase(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice trying to reveal while the commit phase is running\n    error InCommitmentPhase(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice there is no commitment to reveal or to void\n    error NothingToReveal();\n\n    /// @notice there is no commitment to cancel\n    error NoCommitmentToCancel();\n\n    /// @notice an earlier commitment was never revealed; resolve it first\n    error PreviousCommitmentNotRevealed();\n\n    /// @notice the commitment belongs to a different cycle\n    error InvalidCycle(uint64 currentCycleNumber, uint64 commitmentCycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice the revealed chunk does not hash to the head of the chain\n    error CommitmentHashNotMatching();\n\n    /// @notice the player can still reveal, so the commitment cannot be voided\n    error CanStillReveal(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice this identity cannot play this game\n    /// @dev What makes an identity invalid is the GAME's, and it is decided in\n    ///      one place: {UsingCommitReveal-_playerOf}. In the base's default,\n    ///      an address identity, it means an id that is not an account, and in\n    ///      a token game it means a token nobody has put at stake.\n    error InvalidPlayer(uint256 id);\n\n    /// @notice the player's reserve cannot cover this\n    error ReserveTooLow(uint256 current, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice the revealed chunk costs more than the bond still set aside\n    error BondTooLow(uint256 bond, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice this reveal carries more actions than one transaction may\n    /// @dev The chunk is what makes a reveal's worst case CALCULABLE, on every\n    ///      chain and whatever a game puts at stake, which is what lets a client\n    ///      pass a real gas limit instead of a guess. A final chunk allowed to\n    ///      be any length would give that back: the bound would hold for every\n    ///      reveal except the last one of every turn.\n    error TooManyActions(uint256 length, uint256 allowed);\n\n    /// @notice a reveal that promises more actions did not carry a full chunk\n    /// @dev LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY. Without it a player dribbles one\n    ///      action per transaction and spreads a turn across an unbounded number\n    ///      of reveals, which is a denial of service on the reveal phase and on\n    ///      everyone else's reads of the board. A chunk that promises a\n    ///      successor must therefore be exactly full; only the LAST one may be\n    ///      short.\n    error InvalidFurtherActions(uint256 length, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice a chunk size of zero, which would make every turn unrevealable\n    /// @dev Same class as a zero phase duration and refused in the same place:\n    ///      it is a deployment mistake whose cost is the first player's stake\n    ///      rather than a revert anybody sees.\n    error InvalidActionsPerReveal();\n\n    /// @notice this game's cycle is advanced by the clock and by nothing else\n    /// @dev A purely timed cycle needs no transaction at all - it simply is\n    ///      what the clock says - so there is nothing for a caller to do here\n    ///      and pretending otherwise would let one look like it had.\n    error NextPhaseNotAllowed();\n\n    /// @notice the phase durations do not describe a cycle this game can run\n    /// @dev Both phases must be non-zero on a timed policy, and both must be\n    ///      zero on a manual one. See {UsingCommitReveal} for why a zero phase\n    ///      is not a configuration but a hole: it makes a commitment either\n    ///      impossible to make or impossible to open.\n    error InvalidCycleConfiguration();\n\n    /// @notice nobody is being waited for, so unanimity has no denominator\n    /// @dev Early advance needs a closed set of members. \"Everyone has\n    ///      committed\" is not a question that can be answered under open\n    ///      entry, and answering it against an empty set would let one caller\n    ///      spin the cycle forward on their own.\n    error NoOneToWaitFor();\n\n    /// @notice this identity has not entered the game, so it cannot take a turn\n    /// @dev What entering MEANS is the game's: a funded reserve here, custody of\n    ///      a token elsewhere. What the cycle needs is only that the set of\n    ///      players who may commit is the same set unanimity is measured\n    ///      against - see {UsingCommitReveal-_makeCommitment}.\n    error NotInGame(uint256 player);\n\n    /// @notice cannot stop being a member while a turn of yours is still open\n    error CommitmentStillOpen(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice some of the members the cycle waits for have not committed yet\n    error StillWaitingToCommit(uint64 committed, uint64 waitedFor);\n\n    /// @notice some of this cycle's commitments have not been revealed yet\n    error StillWaitingToReveal(uint64 revealed, uint64 committed);\n\n    /// @notice this game has open entry, so it has no roster to act on\n    error NoRoster();\n\n    /// @notice this game's roster was already opened\n    error RosterAlreadyOpened();\n\n    /// @notice a roster needs a creator, who is the only one who can start it\n    error InvalidCreator();\n\n    /// @notice a roster must hold at least two members\n    error InvalidSeats(uint8 seats);\n\n    /// @notice a game for a fixed set of members plays at least one cycle\n    error InvalidCycles(uint16 cycles);\n\n    /// @notice this game has played its last cycle: no commitment, advance or\n    ///         forfeit any more\n    error GameEnded(uint64 lastCycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice the game has started, so its roster is closed\n    error GameAlreadyStarted();\n\n    /// @notice every seat of this game is taken\n    error GameFull(uint8 seats);\n\n    /// @notice a game starts with at least two members seated\n    error NotEnoughMembers(uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice this member has acted in the current phase, so the creator\n    ///         cannot forfeit them\n    error MemberHasActed(uint256 player, uint64 cycleNumber);\n}\n","keccak256":"0x96821d387ae97a88ea2e7e6fa021d2b42e3151fa4ed2f38cd00e82f9d69928cf","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealEvents.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealTypes} from \"./UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol\";\n\n/// @title The events of the commit-reveal base\n/// @dev Emitted by {CommitReveal} and {UsingCommitReveal} through qualified\n///      names, and inherited by a game's own events interface so that they are\n///      in the game's ABI where a client looks for them.\n///\n///      `player` IS A `uint256` IN EVERY EVENT HERE, and it is the same\n///      `uint256` the store keys by: whatever the game means by a player\n///      (an account widened, an avatar's token id), never an address that a\n///      token game would have to truncate into.\n///\n///      NO EVENT HERE CARRIES A GAME'S ACTIONS. The base never sees them: a\n///      game emits what its actions did in events of its own, and a reader\n///      wanting whole turns stitches the chunk events below on\n///      `furtherActions`.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealEvents is UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice A player topped up the reserve they are willing to risk.\n    event ReserveDeposited(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint256 amountAdded,\n        uint256 newAmount\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player took tokens back out of their reserve.\n    event ReserveWithdrawn(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint256 amountRemoved,\n        uint256 newAmount\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player committed to a turn for this cycle.\n    event CommitmentMade(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player withdrew their commitment before the reveal phase.\n    event CommitmentCancelled(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player revealed a chunk of what they had committed to.\n    /// @param commitmentHash The head this reveal opened, which for the second\n    ///        and later chunks of a turn is not the hash that was committed.\n    /// @param furtherActions The new head, or zero when this completed the turn.\n    /// @param cost What the game's resolution reported this chunk cost, taken\n    ///        from the bond and from the reserve.\n    event CommitmentRevealed(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 cost\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A missed reveal was settled, in whole or by one chunk.\n    /// @dev ONE EVENT FOR BOTH ROUTES, shaped like {CommitmentRevealed} because\n    ///      a settlement shown the chunks walks the chain exactly as a reveal\n    ///      does. A settlement WITHOUT them closes the commitment in one call\n    ///      and reports a zero `furtherActions`.\n    /// @param cycleNumber The cycle in progress when it was settled.\n    /// @param commitmentHash The head this settlement opened or closed.\n    /// @param furtherActions The new head, or zero when the commitment is now\n    ///        closed and any surplus of its bond is reserve again.\n    /// @param forfeited How much the game's {UsingCommitReveal-_forfeit} took,\n    ///        in the units of the bond. A game whose stake is not a bond (an\n    ///        avatar in custody) reports zero here and says what it took in an\n    ///        event of its own.\n    event CommitmentVoid(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 forfeited\n    );\n\n    /// @notice The cycle moved because somebody pushed it, rather than because\n    ///         the clock said so.\n    /// @dev A clock-driven turnover emits nothing, because nothing happened on\n    ///      chain: that is the difference this event exists to make visible.\n    event CycleAdvanced(\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting,\n        address pushedBy\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A closed roster was opened: the game now has `seats` seats, a\n    ///         creator who starts it, and plays `cycles` cycles from its start.\n    /// @param gameOptions What the game's own rules read at this table,\n    ///        opaque to the base (see {UsingCommitReveal-_gameOptions}).\n    event RosterOpened(\n        address indexed creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 gameOptions\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A member took a seat, by funding a reserve.\n    /// @param seated How many seats are taken now.\n    event SeatTaken(uint256 indexed player, uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice A member left their seat: by emptying their reserve, or by\n    ///         being forfeited.\n    /// @param seated How many seats are taken now.\n    event SeatReleased(uint256 indexed player, uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice The creator started the game, which closes its roster.\n    /// @dev Followed by {CycleAdvanced} in the same transaction: starting\n    ///      re-anchors the clock, so the first cycle runs its full length.\n    /// @param lastCycleNumber The last cycle it plays: after it, the game has\n    ///        ended.\n    event GameStarted(\n        address indexed creator,\n        uint256 members,\n        uint64 lastCycleNumber\n    );\n\n    /// @notice The creator forfeited a member who had not acted in the\n    ///         current phase: the cycle stops waiting for them, for good.\n    event MemberForfeited(uint256 indexed player, uint64 indexed cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice The cycle started, or stopped, waiting for this player.\n    /// @param waitedFor Whether it now waits for them.\n    /// @param waitedForCount How many members it waits for in total, which is\n    ///        the denominator unanimity is measured against.\n    event WaitedForChanged(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        bool waitedFor,\n        uint64 waitedForCount\n    );\n}\n","keccak256":"0x9ea182c433fe84b1f3320d9e363cab60ba8b0c746180f5780143f021aedaff30","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {ITime} from \"solidity-kit/solc_0_8/debug/time/interfaces/ITime.sol\";\n\n/// @title The types of the commit-reveal base\n/// @notice Everything the mechanism means by a cycle, a commitment and a tally,\n///         and nothing a game means by an action.\n/// @dev A game's own types interface INHERITS this one, so its code and its\n///      ABI keep naming `Cycle` and `Commitment` unqualified, exactly as they\n///      did when these lived in the game. The base never sees an action type:\n///      a game's routes are typed (`reveal(player, Placement[] calldata, ...)`)\n///      and hand the base a digest and a count. See {UsingCommitReveal}.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice HOW THE CYCLE ADVANCES. One of three, chosen by the deployment.\n    /// @dev It used to be derived rather than declared: a game whose two phase\n    ///      durations were both zero was a manual game, AND was a game that\n    ///      skipped the commit phase, because one flag stood for both. Two\n    ///      independent things behind one derivation is what made this look\n    ///      like a mode instead of a policy, so the policy is now said out loud\n    ///      and the commit phase is never skipped by anybody.\n    ///\n    ///      `Timed` needs no transaction at all: the cycle simply is what the\n    ///      clock says. The other two are advanced by an `advanceCycle` route,\n    ///      which is permissionless and strictly conditional - it may only do\n    ///      what the rules already permit, so letting anyone call it grants\n    ///      nothing.\n    enum CyclePolicy {\n        /// @notice The clock decides, and nothing else can.\n        Timed,\n        /// @notice There is no clock. The cycle moves when the players have all\n        ///         acted and someone pushes it.\n        Manual,\n        /// @notice The clock decides the DEADLINE, and unanimity can bring the\n        ///         next phase forward. Never the other way round: see\n        ///         {UsingCommitReveal-_advanceCycle}.\n        TimedWithEarlyAdvance\n    }\n\n    /// @notice What the mechanism is configured with. A game's own config\n    ///         carries these plus whatever its actions need (a token, a cost).\n    struct CommitRevealConfig {\n        uint256 startTime;\n        uint256 commitPhaseDuration;\n        uint256 revealPhaseDuration;\n        ITime time;\n        /// @notice THE CHUNK: how many actions one reveal transaction may carry.\n        /// @dev A DEPLOYMENT PARAMETER AND NOT A CONSTANT, because the two things\n        ///      that decide it are both outside the framework: how expensive one\n        ///      action is to resolve (the game's) and what fits in a transaction\n        ///      (the chain's). Zero is refused at construction: it would make\n        ///      every turn unrevealable, which costs the first player their stake\n        ///      rather than reverting anything.\n        uint256 actionsPerReveal;\n        CyclePolicy cyclePolicy;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHERE THE CYCLE IS, and until when.\n    /// @dev The client reads this rather than computing it, because under\n    ///      {CyclePolicy-TimedWithEarlyAdvance} the arithmetic alone cannot\n    ///      know that a phase was brought forward - that takes a transaction.\n    ///      A local clock predicts this correctly right up until someone\n    ///      advances early, which is exactly why the prediction is a floor and\n    ///      this is the answer.\n    struct Cycle {\n        uint64 cycleNumber;\n        /// @notice true in the commit phase, false in the reveal phase\n        bool commiting;\n        /// @notice chain time the current phase opened\n        /// @dev ZERO MEANS THERE IS NO CLOCK (a Manual game), not \"the cycle\".\n        uint64 phaseStart;\n        /// @notice chain time the current phase closes, if nobody advances it\n        /// @dev Zero means there is no clock. Under an early advance this is\n        ///      the phase's NOMINAL end, unmoved: an advance widens a window\n        ///      and never shortens one, which is what keeps a reveal scheduled\n        ///      against the nominal time valid.\n        uint64 phaseEnd;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHO THE CYCLE IS WAITING FOR, and how many have acted.\n    /// @dev `waitedFor` is the denominator unanimity is measured against, and\n    ///      it is deliberately NOT the number of players who are alive: a game\n    ///      may keep a silent player in the world while no longer blocking on\n    ///      them. What it costs to stop being waited for is the game's, and it\n    ///      is a separate question from this count.\n    struct Attendance {\n        uint64 waitedFor;\n        /// @notice how many of them have committed IN THE CURRENT CYCLE\n        uint64 committed;\n        /// @notice how many of those commitments have been revealed\n        uint64 revealed;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice What an advance has written down, if anything.\n    /// @dev STORAGE ONLY. Read {Cycle} instead; this is the raw anchor it is\n    ///      computed from, and every field means something different per\n    ///      policy, which is why it is not the thing anyone else reads.\n    struct CycleState {\n        /// @notice the cycle the anchor names; zero means nothing has advanced\n        ///         yet, so the anchor is (cycle 2, START_TIME, commit phase)\n        uint64 anchorCycleNumber;\n        /// @notice chain time the anchor cycle's COMMIT phase opened (timed\n        ///         policies only)\n        uint64 anchoredAt;\n        /// @notice the cycle whose reveal phase was opened early, if any\n        uint64 earlyRevealCycleNumber;\n        /// @notice when that happened, which is when that reveal window opened\n        uint64 earlyRevealAt;\n        /// @notice which phase the anchor cycle is in (Manual only; the timed\n        ///         policies read it off the clock)\n        bool commiting;\n        /// @notice the last cycle a game with an end plays, written by\n        ///         {CommitReveal-start}; zero means no end (the persistent\n        ///         world, and a table before its start)\n        /// @dev IN THIS SLOT ON PURPOSE: it shares the slot {commiting} is\n        ///      in, which every read of the cycle loads already, so a commit\n        ///      that checks the end reads nothing new.\n        uint64 lastCycleNumber;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice How many members have acted, in the cycle it names.\n    /// @dev The cycle is stored WITH the counts so that one slot can serve\n    ///      every cycle: a tally whose cycle is not the current one is a tally\n    ///      of zero, and the first player to act in a new cycle resets it.\n    struct CycleTally {\n        uint64 cycleNumber;\n        uint64 committed;\n        uint64 revealed;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice A CLOSED ROSTER: a game for a fixed set of members, created by\n    ///         anyone, joined by staking, started by its creator.\n    /// @dev OPT-IN BY INITIALISATION. A game whose storage never had a roster\n    ///      written (`seats` zero, the persistent world) has OPEN ENTRY and\n    ///      behaves exactly as it did before rosters existed: a funded\n    ///      reserve is a member, at any time. See\n    ///      {UsingCommitReveal-_openRoster}.\n    struct Roster {\n        /// @notice who created the game, and may start it and forfeit a\n        ///         member who has not acted\n        address creator;\n        /// @notice how many members it may hold; zero means open entry\n        uint8 seats;\n        /// @notice whether the creator has started it, which closes the roster\n        bool started;\n        /// @notice how many cycles it plays from its start; never zero under a\n        ///         roster, since every game for a fixed set of members ends\n        uint16 cycles;\n        /// @notice how many members were seated when it started, which those\n        ///         who leave afterwards do not change (zero before the start)\n        uint8 startedWith;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice THE HEAD OF A HASH CHAIN, plus what is riding on it.\n    /// @dev `hash` is the hash of the NEXT chunk of the turn still owed, which\n    ///      for a turn that fits in one transaction is simply the whole turn. A\n    ///      reveal rewrites it to the chunk after that, and the commitment stays\n    ///      open until a chunk arrives declaring no further actions.\n    ///\n    ///      `bond` FALLS AS THE CHAIN IS WALKED, by what each chunk costs as it\n    ///      lands, so what is left earmarked is what the REST of the turn is\n    ///      still holding. It may be MORE than the rest will cost: a bond equal\n    ///      to the exact cost would tell everyone how many actions the\n    ///      commitment hides, because it is public. The surplus is released\n    ///      when the turn closes, by its last reveal or by a settlement shown\n    ///      the chunks. See {UsingCommitReveal-_openMissedChunk}.\n    struct Commitment {\n        bytes24 hash;\n        uint64 cycleNumber;\n        /// @notice reserve earmarked for what this commitment has NOT yet\n        ///         revealed\n        uint256 bond;\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xe0156b51cbe97ee9dfa1e285dd1c65ac36d35383b8aeef94ed5a0d5db6062a8b","license":"MIT"},"project/src/game/interfaces/IGame.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\n// The delegation surface is NOT restated here. It is composed from the\n// interface that ships beside the implementation in the etherplay delegation\n// package, so the router's selector list and the library cannot drift: a\n// restatement is a copy, and the failure it produces is a selector that routes\n// nowhere, which reads to a player as a broken wallet rather than as a missing\n// feature.\nimport {IDelegation} from \"@etherplay/delegation/contracts/IDelegation.sol\";\n\nimport {ICommitRevealLobby} from \"../../commit-reveal/interfaces/ICommitRevealLobby.sol\";\n\nimport \"./UsingGameTypes.sol\";\nimport \"./UsingGameEvents.sol\";\nimport \"./UsingGameErrors.sol\";\n\n/// @dev EVERY `player` HERE IS A `uint256`, and it is the identity rather than\n///      an account: what this game means by a player is decided in exactly one\n///      place, {UsingCommitReveal-_playerOf}. In this game it is an ARMY\n///      (`CONTEXT.md`): an id above `type(uint160).max`, so that army ids and\n///      the address-derived ids of accounts can never collide. An army id is\n///      `nonce << 160 | owner`, the owner's `nonce`th army, so the client can\n///      name the army its next deployment creates before committing it. See\n///      `web/src/lib/game/identity.ts` for the client's half of the same rule.\ninterface IGameCommit is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Take tokens back out of the CALLER'S ACCOUNT reserve.\n    /// @dev Deliberately NOT delegable: a delegate may spend the reserve on\n    ///      playing and may never withdraw it. And it only ever reaches an\n    ///      account's reserve, because an army id is never an address: an\n    ///      army's reserve IS its stake and leaves only through the game.\n    ///      Settles the caller's most recent deployment first\n    ///      ({settleDeployment}), so a failed one's refund can be withdrawn.\n    function withdrawFromReserve(uint256 amount) external;\n\n    /// @notice Write the refund of `army`'s failed deployment: its stake goes\n    ///         back to its owner's ACCOUNT reserve, and it is no longer waited\n    ///         for. Anyone may call it, once the deployment's cycle is over.\n    /// @return refunded What moved; zero (and nothing happens) if the army's\n    ///         deployment did not fail, or its refund is already written.\n    /// @dev A deployment fails when another reveals the same spawn point in\n    ///      its cycle, or its footprint is not clear (a piece on it at the start\n    ///      of the cycle, or one arriving on it during it). Nothing runs when a\n    ///      cycle ends, so the refund waits for this call; the owner's next\n    ///      deployment and withdrawal make it for their most recent army.\n    function settleDeployment(uint256 army) external returns (uint256 refunded);\n\n    /// @notice Commit to this cycle's submission for `player`.\n    /// @param player The army the commitment is FOR (zero for the caller's own\n    ///        account, which only a table seats). Must be one the caller may act\n    ///        for: its owner, or a delegate of its owner.\n    /// @dev A COMMITMENT FOR AN ARMY THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET IS ITS DEPLOYMENT,\n    ///      and it creates it: `player` must be the owner's next army id\n    ///      ({IGameGetters-getNextArmy}), the stake moves from the owner's\n    ///      account reserve into the new army's reserve, and the army becomes a\n    ///      waited-for member, committed in this same cycle. Its reveal names\n    ///      the spawn point.\n    function makeCommitment(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond,\n        address payable payee\n    ) external payable;\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw a commitment before the reveal phase begins.\n    /// @dev Cancelling a DEPLOYMENT is free: the army's whole stake goes back\n    ///      to its owner's account reserve, and the cycle stops waiting for\n    ///      the army, which never exists on the board.\n    function cancelCommitment(uint256 player) external;\n\n    // The settlements of a missed reveal and the advance live on the commit\n    // route rather than the reveal route only for SIZE: the reveal route holds\n    // the whole move rule and has no room left under the 24,576-byte limit.\n\n    /// @notice Settle one chunk of a missed reveal by showing it.\n    /// @dev Anyone may call it. A missed DEPLOYMENT forfeits the whole stake,\n    ///      which is burned; a missed pass forfeits nothing here\n    ///      (`docs/adr/0005-missed-reveal-freezes-the-army.md` is what a missed\n    ///      move costs, and it is not this route's).\n    function acknowledgeMissedReveal(\n        uint256 player,\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        bytes32 secret,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) external;\n\n    /// @notice Settle a missed reveal WITHOUT its chunks, forfeiting the whole\n    ///         bond still earmarked for it (for a missed deployment, the whole\n    ///         stake, burned). Only the owner or their delegate.\n    function forfeitMissedReveal(uint256 player) external;\n\n    /// @notice Move the cycle on, if the rules already permit it. See the base.\n    /// @dev First stops waiting for every dead army (a failed, cancelled or\n    ///      unrevealed deployment), under `Manual` and `TimedWithEarlyAdvance`.\n    function advanceCycle()\n        external\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting);\n}\n\n/// @notice BUYING IN: what `StakeSale` calls with every purchase.\n/// @dev Its own interface (on the `GameTable` route) so the sale names the one\n///      function it calls, for the world and for every table alike.\ninterface IGameStake is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Credit an ACCOUNT's reserve: stake bought, not yet deployed;\n    ///         AT A TABLE, buy a seat: a new army for that account.\n    /// @dev Takes `player` rather than crediting msg.sender, so that the stake\n    ///      can be paid from the wallet holding the funds. Anyone may top up\n    ///      anyone; only the owner can withdraw.\n    ///\n    ///      AN ACCOUNT RESERVE NEVER MAKES ITS ACCOUNT A MEMBER: only armies are\n    ///      waited for (`docs/adr/0006-stake-erc20-reserve-exit-only.md`).\n    ///      Refuses an army id with {InvalidPlayer}, so nobody can pre-fund a\n    ///      future army or slip extra stake into an existing one.\n    ///\n    ///      AT A TABLE THE SEAT IS THE ARMY. Each purchase of exactly one stake\n    ///      creates a new army owned by `player`'s account, funded with it, on\n    ///      the table's next spawn point: that purchase IS the deployment\n    ///      (`UsingGameTable-_joinTable`). Any other amount reverts\n    ///      {WrongStake}; a started table {GameAlreadyStarted}; a full one\n    ///      {GameFull}.\n    function addToReserve(uint256 player, uint256 amount) external;\n}\n\n/// @notice A TABLE: leaving before it starts, and its payout once it is over\n///         (`work/specs/tasked/infinite-chess.md`, stories 38 to 42).\ninterface IGameTable is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Leave the table before it starts: `army`'s whole stake back\n    ///         to its owner, in tokens, its seat freed and the army removed.\n    /// @dev The owner only, never a delegate, like {IGameCommit-withdrawFromReserve}.\n    ///      The one exception to \"an army's reserve is never withdrawn\"\n    ///      (`docs/adr/0006-stake-erc20-reserve-exit-only.md`): before the\n    ///      start nothing has been played. Reverts {GameAlreadyStarted} after.\n    function leaveTable(uint256 army) external returns (uint256 amount);\n\n    /// @notice Count up to `maxSteps` steps of the material on the board at\n    ///         the cap, and say whether the count is complete. Anyone may call\n    ///         it, once the table's last cycle is over.\n    /// @dev Only needed when the count is too big for one {claim}, which runs\n    ///      whatever is left of it first.\n    function tally(uint256 maxSteps) external returns (bool done);\n\n    /// @notice Pay `army`'s share of the table's stakes, in ETH, to its\n    ///         current owner, through the token's minter (`StakeSale.redeem`).\n    ///         Anyone may call it, once per army.\n    /// @dev The table is over once one king stands (it takes every stake) or\n    ///      once its last cycle is over (every standing army takes a share in\n    ///      proportion to its material: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5,\n    ///      queen 9; evenly between the standing kings if none has any).\n    ///      Reverts {TableNotOver} before, {NothingToClaim} for an army owed\n    ///      nothing, {AlreadyPaid} the second time.\n    function claim(uint256 army) external returns (uint256 paid);\n\n    /// @notice The table's outcome as it stands: whether it is over, the last\n    ///         king standing (zero if none), and once settled, every stake on\n    ///         it and the material counted at the cap.\n    function getTableOutcome() external view returns (TableOutcome memory);\n\n    /// @notice What {claim} pays `army` once the outcome is written (by the\n    ///         first claim), zero before or if it is owed nothing; and whether\n    ///         it was paid.\n    function getTableShare(\n        uint256 army\n    ) external view returns (uint256 share, bool paid);\n}\n\ninterface IGameReveal is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Reveal one chunk of what an army committed to, and apply it.\n    /// @dev Takes `player` rather than using msg.sender so that anyone can\n    ///      reveal for them. A CALLER RESUMES FROM THE CHAIN, NOT FROM MEMORY:\n    ///      see the base.\n    ///\n    ///      An army whose deployment is not revealed yet reveals that\n    ///      deployment, which this forwards to\n    ///      {IGameDeploymentReveal-revealDeployment}. Any other submission\n    ///      is a pass (no move) or exactly ONE move of one of the army's\n    ///      pieces, legal on the board as it stood at the START of the cycle\n    ///      ({IGameSimulation-legalMoves}); anything else reverts\n    ///      {OneMovePerCycle} or {IllegalMove}.\n    function reveal(\n        uint256 player,\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        bytes32 secret,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        address payable payee\n    ) external payable;\n}\n\ninterface IGameDeploymentReveal is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Reveal an army's deployment, committed this cycle: exactly one\n    ///         move, from and to the spawn point, which must have been open at\n    ///         the START of the cycle.\n    /// @dev {IGameReveal-reveal} for the one submission that is a deployment,\n    ///      on a route of its own for size alone. Reverts {InvalidDeployment}\n    ///      for an army that is not deploying.\n    function revealDeployment(\n        uint256 player,\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        bytes32 secret,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        address payable payee\n    ) external payable;\n}\n\ninterface IGameExit is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice Pay an exited army's whole stake, in ETH, to its owner.\n    /// @dev Anyone may call it, once the cycle in which its king landed alone\n    ///      on an exit has closed: the army left the board then, and this only\n    ///      PAYS. Its reserve and that of every army whose stake it took\n    ///      (down the tree of captures, a stone's excepted) are debited and\n    ///      the sum is redeemed at `StakeSale`'s fixed price for its owner.\n    ///      Reverts {NotExited} before, and {AlreadyPaid} once paid. A tree too\n    ///      big for one transaction is first {collect}ed.\n    function exit(uint256 army) external returns (uint256 paid);\n\n    /// @notice Collect up to `maxArmies` armies of an exited army's tree of\n    ///         captured stakes towards its payout, and say whether the whole tree is collected.\n    /// @dev Permissionless and incremental, for a tree too big for one\n    ///      transaction; never needed to have exited, only to be paid in one go.\n    function collect(\n        uint256 army,\n        uint256 maxArmies\n    ) external returns (bool done);\n\n    /// @notice Whether `army` has left the board through an exit, as of now.\n    function isExited(uint256 army) external view returns (bool);\n}\n\ninterface IGameGetters is UsingGameTypes {\n    function getCycleNumber()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting);\n\n    /// @notice Where the cycle is, and until when. THE ONE A CLIENT SHOULD READ.\n    function getCycle() external view returns (Cycle memory cycle);\n\n    /// @notice Who the cycle is waiting for, and how many have acted.\n    function getAttendance()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (Attendance memory attendance);\n\n    function getCommitment(\n        uint256 player\n    ) external view returns (Commitment memory commitment);\n\n    function getReserve(uint256 player) external view returns (uint256 amount);\n\n    function getConfig() external view returns (Config memory config);\n\n    /// @notice How many piece-moves a move holds at most here: 3, or 1 at a\n    ///         table whose creator turned three piece-moves off (one bit of\n    ///         its `gameOptions`, `docs/adr/0016`). 3 in both worlds.\n    /// @dev What the reveal caps a move at. The client passes it to the\n    ///      simulation routes ({IGameSimulation-isLegalWholeMove},\n    ///      {IGameSimulation-legalMovesAlongside}), which read nothing.\n    function getMaxPieceMoves() external view returns (uint256 maxPieceMoves);\n\n    /// @notice Every piece on the squares from (`minX`,`minY`) to\n    ///         (`maxX`,`maxY`) inclusive, RESOLVED, plus the cycle the answer\n    ///         is for.\n    /// @dev The client reads the board through this and nothing else, and only\n    ///      the area in view: there is no indexer for state\n    ///      (`docs/adr/0007-rules-live-only-in-the-contract.md`). What is stored\n    ///      is the cycle's accumulated facts, so the board is worked out here,\n    ///      lazily (`docs/adr/0002-order-free-lazy-resolution.md`).\n    function getPieces(\n        int32 minX,\n        int32 minY,\n        int32 maxX,\n        int32 maxY\n    ) external view returns (Piece[] memory pieces, uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice WHAT THE LAST CLOSED CYCLE DID inside a rectangle of the board,\n    ///         bounds inclusive: every square where a piece was captured or\n    ///         pieces died in a collision, in no meaningful order.\n    /// @return outcomes one entry per such square\n    /// @return cycleNumber the cycle they happened in: the one before the\n    ///         current cycle\n    /// @dev Read from the same accumulated facts as {getPieces}, which a\n    ///      square keeps until a reveal of a later cycle touches it. So the\n    ///      answer is complete during the next commit phase, and during its\n    ///      reveal phase it can only LOSE squares, never report a wrong one: a\n    ///      reader that wants the whole picture keeps the union of what it read\n    ///      for the same `cycleNumber`.\n    function getOutcomes(\n        int32 minX,\n        int32 minY,\n        int32 maxX,\n        int32 maxY\n    )\n        external\n        view\n        returns (SquareOutcome[] memory outcomes, uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice The spawn points a deployment committed now may reveal: the\n    ///         free ones nearest the origin, in spiral order, as they stood at\n    ///         the start of the current cycle.\n    function getOpenSpawnPoints()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint64[] memory spawnPoints, uint64 cycleNumber);\n}\n\n/// @dev THE ARMY REGISTRY, resolved through every capture: whether each army\n///      stands, and what it holds. Its own route because resolving a stake\n///      walks the captures not yet folded (`docs/adr/0013`), and that does not\n///      fit beside the board reads.\ninterface IGameRegistry is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice One army, resolved.\n    function getArmy(uint256 army) external view returns (ArmyView memory);\n\n    /// @notice THE ARMY REGISTRY, a page at a time, resolved: every army ever\n    ///         created, in the order they were.\n    function getArmies(\n        uint256 offset,\n        uint256 limit\n    ) external view returns (ArmyView[] memory armies, uint256 total);\n\n    /// @notice Every army `owner` has created, resolved.\n    /// @dev Every army is played by the account that created it.\n    function getArmiesOf(\n        address owner\n    ) external view returns (ArmyView[] memory armies);\n\n    /// @notice The id `owner`'s next deployment creates.\n    function getNextArmy(address owner) external view returns (uint256 army);\n\n    /// @notice Whether `army` is FROZEN by a missed reveal: it never moves\n    ///         again and its king cannot exit, but it can still be captured\n    ///         (`docs/adr/0005-missed-reveal-freezes-the-army.md`).\n    /// @dev A DEFINITION, NOT JUST A FLAG: an army landed on the board whose\n    ///      missed reveal has been settled, OR which holds an unrevealed\n    ///      commitment from a cycle that is over, so it is frozen from the\n    ///      moment its reveal window closes, before anybody settles it. A\n    ///      deployment never revealed is not frozen: it has no army to freeze,\n    ///      and its stake is burned instead.\n    function isFrozen(uint256 army) external view returns (bool);\n}\n\ninterface IGameSimulation is UsingGameTypes {\n    /// @notice The pieces an army deployed at `spawnPoint` stands on, by the\n    ///         rule the board is resolved with, and with nothing read or\n    ///         written.\n    /// @dev A client runs it from the deployed bytecode in its own sandbox\n    ///      (`web/src/lib/game/simulation/`) to show where a planned army will\n    ///      stand, so the preview is the rule and not a copy of it.\n    function previewDeployment(\n        uint64 spawnPoint,\n        uint256 army\n    ) external view returns (Piece[] memory pieces);\n\n    /// @notice Every square the piece on `from` may move to, by the rule the\n    ///         reveal applies, judged against `board`: the board as it stood at\n    ///         the start of the cycle, as {IGameGetters-getPieces} returns it.\n    ///         Empty if `board` has nothing on `from`.\n    /// @dev Reads nothing: the client runs it in its sandbox to highlight a\n    ///      selected piece's legal destinations, so the highlight is the rule\n    ///      and not a copy of it. It only judges what `board` holds, so pass it\n    ///      every piece within reach (8 squares around `from` is enough: the\n    ///      slider range is 7 and a king looks one square past its\n    ///      destination).\n    function legalMoves(\n        Piece[] calldata board,\n        uint64 from\n    ) external pure returns (uint64[] memory destinations);\n\n    /// @notice Whether `moves` is a legal move for `army`, by the rule the\n    ///         reveal applies, judged against `board` (the board as it stood\n    ///         at the start of the cycle, as {IGameGetters-getPieces} returns\n    ///         it): at most `maxPieceMoves` piece-moves, none moving one piece\n    ///         twice, no two to one square, and each by one of `army`'s pieces\n    ///         and legal with the move's own vacated squares counted as empty\n    ///         (`docs/adr/0016`). An empty move, a pass, is legal. The order\n    ///         `moves` lists them in changes nothing.\n    /// @param maxPieceMoves the move's cap: 3, or 1 at a table that turns\n    ///        three piece-moves off. A PARAMETER because this reads nothing,\n    ///        so it cannot read a table's options.\n    /// @dev Reads nothing: the client runs it in its sandbox to refuse a\n    ///      planned move before it is committed, so the refusal is the rule\n    ///      and not a copy of it. Pass every piece within reach of every\n    ///      piece-move, as for {legalMoves}.\n    function isLegalWholeMove(\n        Piece[] calldata board,\n        uint256 army,\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        uint256 maxPieceMoves\n    ) external pure returns (bool legal);\n\n    /// @notice Every square the piece on `from` may move to as one more\n    ///         piece-move of a move that already holds `others`: exactly the\n    ///         `to` for which {isLegalWholeMove} accepts `others` plus\n    ///         `from` to `to`, for the army of the piece on `from`. So it\n    ///         counts the squares `others` vacate as empty, offers nothing if\n    ///         the move is full or `others` is not legal, and never a square\n    ///         one of `others` goes to. Empty if `board` has nothing on\n    ///         `from`; {legalMoves} when `others` is empty (at any cap of one or\n    ///         more).\n    /// @dev Reads nothing: a planner runs it in its sandbox to offer a piece's\n    ///      destinations alongside the piece-moves already planned.\n    function legalMovesAlongside(\n        Piece[] calldata board,\n        uint64 from,\n        Move[] calldata others,\n        uint256 maxPieceMoves\n    ) external pure returns (uint64[] memory destinations);\n\n    /// @notice What a piece of `kind` is worth in material: pawn 1, knight 3,\n    ///         bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, and nothing for a king or an empty\n    ///         square. The figure a table's payout splits its stakes by.\n    /// @dev Reads nothing: the offline world's machine seats run it in their\n    ///      sandbox to rank what they can capture, so their scoring is the\n    ///      contract's table and not a copy of it.\n    function materialOf(PieceKind kind) external pure returns (uint256);\n}\n\ninterface IGame is\n    IGameStake,\n    IGameTable,\n    IGameCommit,\n    IGameReveal,\n    IGameDeploymentReveal,\n    IGameExit,\n    IGameGetters,\n    IGameRegistry,\n    IGameSimulation,\n    IDelegation\n{}\n\n/// @notice A game at a table for a fixed set of players: the whole game, plus\n///         the lobby's routes. What a clone made by {CommitRevealGameFactory}\n///         answers to; the persistent world answers to {IGame} alone.\ninterface IGameLobby is IGame, ICommitRevealLobby {}\n","keccak256":"0xa260de953d0a194d182a35b840b9ca00a17d476efbadb5910724f31c3c0d23c6","license":"AGPL-3.0"},"project/src/game/interfaces/UsingGameErrors.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealErrors} from \"../../commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealErrors.sol\";\n\n/// @dev The mechanism's errors are inherited from the commit-reveal base\n///      (`src/commit-reveal/`). What is declared here is this game's own.\ninterface UsingGameErrors is UsingCommitRevealErrors {\n    /// @notice The deployment parameters cannot make a board: spawn points\n    ///         closer than an army's footprint, or no spawn point ever open.\n    error InvalidSpawnGrid();\n\n    /// @notice A deployment's reveal must hold exactly one `Move` whose `from`\n    ///         and `to` are both the spawn point, in one chunk.\n    error InvalidDeployment();\n\n    /// @notice The position is not on the spawn grid.\n    error NotASpawnPoint(uint64 position);\n\n    /// @notice The spawn point was not open at the start of this cycle.\n    error SpawnPointNotOpen(uint64 position);\n\n    /// @notice The move is not one this army may make on the board as it stood\n    ///         at the start of the cycle.\n    error IllegalMove(uint64 from, uint64 to);\n\n    /// @notice A submission after an army's deployment is ONE move, in one\n    ///         chunk: a pass (nothing) or up to three piece-moves, each by a\n    ///         different piece and none two to one square (`docs/adr/0016`).\n    error OneMovePerCycle();\n    /// @notice The army has not left the board through an exit (yet).\n    error NotExited(uint256 army);\n    /// @notice The exited army's stake was already paid.\n    error AlreadyPaid(uint256 army);\n\n    /// @notice The table was created with `gameOptions` this game cannot read\n    ///         (a bit set other than `ChessRules.ONE_PIECE_MOVE`), so nobody\n    ///         may take a seat at it.\n    error UnreadableGameOptions(bytes32
