A missed pass\n    ///      forfeits nothing here; what a missed move costs is the freeze.\n    function _acknowledgeMissedReveal(\n        uint256 player,\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        bytes32 secret,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal {\n        uint64 committedIn = _commitmentOf(player).cycleNumber;\n        CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk = _openMissedChunk(\n            player,\n            _digest(moves, secret, furtherActions),\n            moves.length,\n            furtherActions\n        );\n        _closeChunk(chunk, _isDeploying(player, committedIn) ? STAKE : 0);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The hash a chunk of moves is committed under.\n    /// @dev ONE ENCODING, ALWAYS, the base's, including for the last chunk,\n    ///      where `furtherActions` is zero and is hashed in anyway. The client\n    ///      builds the same bytes (`web/src/lib/chess/commit-reveal.ts`).\n    function _digest(\n        Move[] calldata moves,\n        bytes32 secret,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal pure returns (bytes24) {\n        return bytes24(keccak256(abi.encode(secret, moves, furtherActions)));\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // RESOLVING\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice THE OPEN SET at the start of `cycleNumber`: the spiral indices\n    ///         of the free spawn points nearest the origin, and the next fresh\n    ///         index after them, and whether that differs from what is\n    ///         stored (which a deployment's reveal then writes).\n    /// @dev See {_openSpawnIndices} for the invariant that makes this K reads.\n    function _openSet(\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (uint64[] memory open, uint64 next, bool changed) {\n        next = _nextSpawnIndex;\n        if (next == 0) {\n            open = new uint64[](OPEN_SPAWN_POINTS);\n            for (uint64 i = 0; i < OPEN_SPAWN_POINTS; i++) open[i] = i;\n            next = OPEN_SPAWN_POINTS;\n            changed = true;\n        } else {\n            open = _openSpawnIndices;\n        }\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < open.length; i++) {\n            (bool landed, ) = _landedBefore(open[i], cycleNumber);\n            if (landed) {\n                open[i] = next;\n                next++;\n                changed = true;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice One army as the registry shows it, resolved for `cycleNumber`.\n    function _armyView(\n        uint256 id,\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (ArmyView memory view_) {\n        ArmyRecord memory army = _armies[id];\n        view_.id = id;\n        if (army.owner == address(0)) return view_;\n        view_.owner = army.owner;\n        view_.deployedIn = army.deployCycle;\n        view_.stake = _reserveOf(id);\n        view_.status = _deploymentStatus(id, cycleNumber);\n        if (army.spawnIndexPlusOne == 0) return view_;\n        view_.spawnPoint = ChessRules.spawnPointAt(\n            army.spawnIndexPlusOne - 1,\n            SPAWN_SPACING\n        );\n        if (view_.status != ArmyStatus.Deployed) return view_;\n        // RESOLVED FROM THE FACTS, like its pieces: what it holds, whichever\n        // squares have been read or folded yet. The stake is the bounded\n        // view's ({_treeStake}).\n        if (_exited(id, cycleNumber)) {\n            view_.status = ArmyStatus.Exited;\n            view_.stake =\n                army.paid\n                    ? 0\n                    : _collected[id] +\n                        _treeStake(id, cycleNumber, STAKE_VIEW_DEPTH);\n            return view_;\n        }\n        view_.king = _kingAt(id, view_.spawnPoint, cycleNumber);\n        view_.stake = _stakeOf(id, cycleNumber);\n        if (_fellIn(id, cycleNumber) != 0) {\n            // Taken: its stake is its taker's, or, a stone's, its own.\n            view_.status = ArmyStatus.Captured;\n            view_.capturedBy = _captureOf(id, cycleNumber);\n            return view_;\n        }\n        // Frozen, it stays on the board with its stake (story 37).\n        if (_isFrozen(id, cycleNumber)) view_.status = ArmyStatus.Frozen;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Every piece on the squares from (`minX`,`minY`) to\n    ///         (`maxX`,`maxY`), resolved for `cycleNumber`.\n    /// @dev TWO SOURCES, NEVER BOTH FOR ONE SQUARE. A square some reveal has\n    ///      touched has a record and is resolved from it ({_squareAt}), found\n    ///      through the zone index; every other square holds what the\n    ///      deployment over it laid there, if one has landed. A square is\n    ///      covered by at most one spawn point's footprint (the spacing is at\n    ///      least the footprint's width), and a footprint reaches at most 3\n    ///      squares left of / below its spawn point and 2 right of / above it,\n    ///      so the spawn points to lay out are those within that margin of the\n    ///      rectangle. The order of the answer depends only on what is on the\n    ///      board, never on the order of the reveals that put it there.\n    function _piecesIn(\n        int32 minX,\n        int32 minY,\n        int32 maxX,\n        int32 maxY,\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (Piece[] memory pieces) {\n        if (maxX < minX || maxY < minY) return new Piece[](0);\n        // A table's armies are hidden until it starts.\n        if (_isBeforeTableStart()) return new Piece[](0);\n        Rect memory rect = Rect(minX, minY, maxX, maxY);\n        uint64[] memory spawnPoints;\n        uint256[] memory armies;\n        (spawnPoints, armies) = _landedAround(rect, cycleNumber);\n        uint64[] memory touched = _touchedIn(rect);\n\n        pieces = new Piece[](\n            spawnPoints.length * ChessRules.ARMY_SIZE + touched.length\n        );\n        uint256 n = 0;\n        for (uint256 k = 0; k < spawnPoints.length; k++) {\n            // A fallen army's pieces have left the board.\n            if (_fellIn(armies[k], cycleNumber) != 0) continue;\n            n = _appendArmy(\n                pieces,\n                n,\n                rect,\n                ChessRules.layout(spawnPoints[k], armies[k])\n            );\n        }\n        for (uint256 k = 0; k < touched.length; k++) {\n            Piece memory piece = _squareAt(touched[k], cycleNumber);\n            if (piece.kind == PieceKind.None) continue;\n            pieces[n] = piece;\n            n++;\n        }\n        assembly {\n            mstore(pieces, n)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The captures and collisions of `cycleNumber` on the squares of\n    ///         the rectangle whose record still holds that cycle's facts.\n    /// @dev See {IGameGetters-getOutcomes}. Only a record OF `cycleNumber` is\n    ///      read, so an older one (an idle square) and a newer one (a reveal of\n    ///      the open cycle) are both skipped, and the resolution is\n    ///      {ChessRules-settle} and {ChessRules-outcome} on the facts the board\n    ///      read folds in, so the two cannot disagree.\n    function _outcomesIn(\n        int32 minX,\n        int32 minY,\n        int32 maxX,\n        int32 maxY,\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (SquareOutcome[] memory outcomes) {\n        if (maxX < minX || maxY < minY) return outcomes;\n        uint64[] memory touched = _touchedIn(Rect(minX, minY, maxX, maxY));\n        outcomes = new SquareOutcome[](touched.length);\n        uint256 n = 0;\n        for (uint256 k = 0; k < touched.length; k++) {\n            SquareRecord storage record = _squares[touched[k]];\n            if (record.cycle != cycleNumber || record.arrivals == 0) continue;\n            (Piece memory captured, uint256 died) = ChessRules.outcome(\n                _standingOf(record, touched[k]),\n                record.departed,\n                record.arrivals,\n                record.kingArrived\n            );\n            if (died == 0 && captured.kind == PieceKind.None) continue;\n            outcomes[n++] = SquareOutcome({\n                position: touched[k],\n                died: uint32(died),\n                captured: captured,\n                piece: _squareAt(touched[k], cycleNumber + 1)\n            });\n        }\n        assembly {\n            mstore(outcomes, n)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The spawn points whose deployment has landed and whose footprint\n    ///      can reach `rect`, and their armies.\n    function _landedAround(\n        Rect memory rect,\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    )\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint64[] memory spawnPoints, uint256[] memory armies)\n    {\n        int256 s = int256(uint256(SPAWN_SPACING));\n        int256 i0 = _ceilDiv(int256(rect.minX) - 2, s);\n        int256 i1 = _floorDiv(int256(rect.maxX) + 2, s);\n        int256 j0 = _ceilDiv(int256(rect.minY) - 2, s);\n        int256 j1 = _floorDiv(int256(rect.maxY) + 2, s);\n        if (i1 < i0 || j1 < j0) return (spawnPoints, armies);\n        uint256 points = uint256((i1 - i0 + 1) * (j1 - j0 + 1));\n        spawnPoints = new uint64[](points);\n        armies = new uint256[](points);\n        uint256 landed = 0;\n        for (int256 j = j0; j <= j1; j++) {\n            for (int256 i = i0; i <= i1; i++) {\n                (bool isLanded, uint256 army) = _landedBefore(\n                    ChessRules.spiralIndex(i, j),\n                    cycleNumber\n                );\n                if (!isLanded) continue;\n                spawnPoints[landed] = PositionUtils.fromXY(\n                    int32(i * s),\n                    int32(j * s)\n                );\n                armies[landed] = army;\n                landed++;\n            }\n        }\n        assembly {\n            mstore(spawnPoints, landed)\n            mstore(armies, landed)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Every square in `rect` that has a record, zone by zone and in the\n    ///      zone index's bit order.\n    function _touchedIn(\n        Rect memory rect\n    ) private view returns (uint64[] memory squares) {\n        int32 zx0 = PositionUtils.zoneCoord(rect.minX);\n        int32 zx1 = PositionUtils.zoneCoord(rect.maxX);\n        int32 zy0 = PositionUtils.zoneCoord(rect.minY);\n        int32 zy1 = PositionUtils.zoneCoord(rect.maxY);\n        uint256 total = 0;\n        uint256 zones = uint256(int256(zx1 - zx0 + 1) * int256(zy1 - zy0 + 1));\n        uint256[] memory bits = new uint256[](zones);\n        uint256 z = 0;\n        for (int32 zy = zy0; zy <= zy1; zy++) {\n            for (int32 zx = zx0; zx <= zx1; zx++) {\n                uint256 b = _touchedSquares[\n                    (uint64(uint32(zy)) << 32) + uint64(uint32(zx))\n                ];\n                bits[z++] = b;\n                for (; b != 0; b &= b - 1) total++;\n            }\n        }\n        squares = new uint64[](total);\n        uint256 n = 0;\n        z = 0;\n        for (int32 zy = zy0; zy <= zy1; zy++) {\n            for (int32 zx = zx0; zx <= zx1; zx++) {\n                n = _appendZone(squares, n, rect, zx, zy, bits[z++]);\n            }\n        }\n        assembly {\n            mstore(squares, n)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Append the squares of zone (`zx`,`zy`) whose bit is set in `b`\n    ///      and that lie in `rect`.\n    function _appendZone(\n        uint64[] memory squares,\n        uint256 n,\n        Rect memory rect,\n        int32 zx,\n        int32 zy,\n        uint256 b\n    ) private pure returns (uint256) {\n        int32 x0 = zx * 16 - 8;\n        int32 y0 = zy * 16 - 8;\n        for (uint256 k = 0; b != 0; k++) {\n            if (b & (uint256(1) << k) == 0) continue;\n            b &= ~(uint256(1) << k);\n            int32 x = x0 + int32(int256(k % 16));\n            int32 y = y0 + int32(int256(k / 16));\n            if (x < rect.minX || x > rect.maxX) continue;\n            if (y < rect.minY || y > rect.maxY) continue;\n            squares[n++] = PositionUtils.fromXY(x, y);\n        }\n        return n;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev A viewport, inclusive on every side.\n    struct Rect {\n        int32 minX;\n        int32 minY;\n        int32 maxX;\n        int32 maxY;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Copy the pieces of `army` that stand inside `rect`, on squares no\n    ///      reveal has touched, to `pieces` from index `n`, and return the\n    ///      index after the last.\n    function _appendArmy(\n        Piece[] memory pieces,\n        uint256 n,\n        Rect memory rect,\n        Piece[] memory army\n    ) private view returns (uint256) {\n        for (uint256 p = 0; p < army.length; p++) {\n            uint64 position = army[p].position;\n            (int32 x, int32 y) = PositionUtils.toXY(position);\n            if (x < rect.minX || x > rect.maxX) continue;\n            if (y < rect.minY || y > rect.maxY) continue;\n            if (_squares[position].cycle != 0) continue;\n            pieces[n] = army[p];\n            n++;\n        }\n        return n;\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x05cc564cbd4ead18b086c78b52c4bc1931bf53d763d8c2f23bfdfadb748cf71e","license":"AGPL-3.0"},"project/src/game/internal/UsingGameStore.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nimport \"../interfaces/UsingGameTypes.sol\";\nimport \"../interfaces/UsingGameErrors.sol\";\nimport {UsingCommitReveal} from \"../../commit-reveal/UsingCommitReveal.sol\";\n\n/// @dev THIS GAME'S STATE, AND ONLY THIS GAME'S. The reserve, the commitments,\n///      the cycle and who it waits for are the commit-reveal base's\n///      (`src/commit-reveal/`), held in its own namespaced storage and reached\n///      through {UsingCommitReveal}; what is declared here is the armies and\n///      the spawn points.\n///\n///      WHAT IS STORED IS FACTS, NOT THE BOARD\n///      (`docs/adr/0002-order-free-lazy-resolution.md`). A reveal only records\n///      what it revealed, by accumulation, and the board (which army stands\n///      where, which deployment landed) is worked out from those facts when it\n///      is read. Nothing is written at the end of a cycle, because nothing runs\n///      then.\nabstract contract UsingGameStore is\n    UsingGameTypes,\n    UsingGameErrors,\n    UsingCommitReveal\n{\n    /// @notice the token players stake\n    IERC20 internal immutable TOKENS;\n    /// @notice what one army holds\n    uint256 internal immutable STAKE;\n    /// @notice the distance between two spawn points on each axis\n    uint32 internal immutable SPAWN_SPACING;\n    /// @notice how many free spawn points are open at once\n    uint8 internal immutable OPEN_SPAWN_POINTS;\n\n    /// @notice What the registry keeps of one army.\n    /// @dev THREE SLOTS, laid out by who reads them (`docs/gas.md`). The first\n    ///      two hold everything a reveal and a commit read: who owns it and\n    ///      where it was deployed, then where its king went and its flags. The\n    ///      third holds what only a capture's fold, an exit's payout and the\n    ///      stake views read. Everything else about an army is RESOLVED from\n    ///      the facts (its status, its king) or is the base's (its reserve,\n    ///      which is its stake).\n    struct ArmyRecord {\n        /// @notice who plays it: the account that created it\n        address owner;\n        /// @notice the cycle its deployment was committed in\n        /// @dev 32 bits so that `index` shares this slot: 2^32 cycles is\n        ///      over a century of one-second cycles. Written through a\n        ///      checked cast ({_cycle32}).\n        uint32 deployCycle;\n        /// @notice the spiral index it revealed, plus one; zero until revealed\n        uint32 spawnIndexPlusOne;\n        /// @notice ITS COMPACT INDEX: its place in `_armyIds`, plus one.\n        /// @dev Written once, when it is created. Storage names an army by\n        ///      this (a square record, a spawn record, `capturedByIndex`) so\n        ///      that those records fit one slot; everything outside storage\n        ///      (the base, events, views) names it by its 256-bit id, which\n        ///      {_armyAt} gives back from the index.\n        uint32 index;\n        // ---- second slot: where its king went, written by its own reveals\n        /// @notice the cycle its king last moved in; zero while it stands\n        ///         where it was deployed\n        uint64 kingMovedIn;\n        /// @notice where that move took it\n        uint64 kingTo;\n        /// @notice where it stood before that move\n        uint64 kingFrom;\n        /// @notice whether its deployment was cancelled in its commit phase\n        bool cancelled;\n        /// @notice whether its king has left the board through an exit, once a\n        ///         later reveal has folded the exit square's facts; false until\n        ///         then (`UsingGameBoard-_exited` reads those facts meanwhile)\n        bool exited;\n        /// @notice whether the exit's payout has started collecting its tree\n        bool collecting;\n        /// @notice whether the exit has been paid\n        bool paid;\n        /// @notice whether a missed reveal of a move has been SETTLED, which\n        ///         froze the army for good; false until somebody settles it\n        ///         (`UsingGameInternal-_isFrozen` also reads the unsettled\n        ///         commitment meanwhile,\n        ///         `docs/adr/0005-missed-reveal-freezes-the-army.md`)\n        bool frozen;\n        /// @notice whether it was created by buying a seat at a TABLE, where\n        ///         exits do nothing and the stake is paid out by the table's\n        ///         end (`UsingGameTable`); in this slot so that every read of\n        ///         `exited` sees it for free\n        bool atTable;\n        /// @notice whether its king has been TAKEN (it is then dead, and its\n        ///         pieces other than a stone read as empty), once a later\n        ///         reveal has folded the square it was taken on; false until\n        ///         then (`UsingGameBoard-_fellIn` reads those facts meanwhile)\n        /// @dev In this slot so that the vanish check of a live army costs\n        ///      this slot and its king's square, nothing more.\n        bool fallen;\n        // ---- third slot: who holds its stake, and when its king fell\n        /// @notice the compact index of the army its stake went to once a\n        ///         later reveal has folded the capture: the army that took its\n        ///         king, or that took its stone; zero until then, for an army\n        ///         whose king was never taken, and for a stone nobody has\n        ///         taken (`docs/adr/0013`, `docs/adr/0014`)\n        /// @dev A CACHE OF A CLOSED CYCLE'S FACTS, written by `_touch` just\n        ///      before it overwrites them (`UsingGameBoard-_captureOf`), or by\n        ///      an exit's collection (`UsingGameInternal-_collect`).\n        uint32 capturedByIndex;\n        /// @notice the cycle its king was taken in, once `fallen` is written;\n        ///         read only to decide whether a capture by this army leaves a\n        ///         stone (`docs/adr/0014`)\n        uint64 fellIn;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice What the reveals have recorded about one square.\n    /// @dev THE PER-SQUARE LAYER, and it holds facts rather than the board\n    ///      (`docs/adr/0002-order-free-lazy-resolution.md`): the piece that\n    ///      stood there at the start of `cycle`, and what `cycle`'s reveals\n    ///      ACCUMULATED about it (the piece leaving, how many pieces arrived,\n    ///      the lone arriver, whether a king arrived). What stands there in any\n    ///      later cycle is {ChessRules-settle} of the two, worked out when the\n    ///      square is read; `cycle` is the LAST TOUCHED cycle, so idle cycles\n    ///      cost nothing. A square no reveal ever touched has no record and\n    ///      reads as the layout of the army deployed over it, if any.\n    ///\n    ///      ONE SLOT: every army in it is a compact index\n    ///      ({ArmyRecord-index}), never a 256-bit id, so a touch writes one\n    ///      slot (`docs/gas.md`). The ARRIVER is the\n    ///      first piece other than a king to arrive, and the KING is kept apart\n    ///      from it, because the king rows of the collision table need both:\n    ///      who the king met when it met exactly one piece\n    ///      (`docs/adr/0003-collision-table-king-survives-a-crowd.md`).\n    struct SquareRecord {\n        uint64 cycle;\n        PieceKind kind;\n        bool departed;\n        uint32 arrivals;\n        bool kingArrived;\n        PieceKind arriverKind;\n        /// @dev the standing piece's army, as an index\n        uint32 armyIndex;\n        /// @dev the arriver's army, as an index\n        uint32 arriverIndex;\n        /// @dev the arriving king's army, as an index\n        uint32 kingIndex;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice What the deployments revealed onto one spawn point add up to.\n    /// @dev ACCUMULATED: `count` is how many deployments revealed it in\n    ///      `cycle`, and `armyIndex` (the army's compact index, so the record is\n    ///      one slot) is meaningful only when that count is one, which\n    ///      is what makes it order-free (see `_revealDeployment`).\n    ///\n    ///      `blocked` is whether its FOOTPRINT (the squares its layout puts a\n    ///      piece on) was not clear in `cycle`: a piece stood on one at the\n    ///      start of the cycle, or arrived on one during it. `arrivedIn` is the\n    ///      last cycle a piece arrived on the footprint, whether or not anyone\n    ///      was deploying here then: it is how an arrival revealed BEFORE the\n    ///      cycle's first deployment reveal is still seen by it. Both are only\n    ///      ever set, never cleared within a cycle, so they are order-free (see\n    ///      `_markArrival`).\n    ///\n    ///      A deployment LANDS when its cycle is over, the count is one and the\n    ///      footprint was not blocked. Once one has landed the record is final:\n    ///      the spawn point is never open again. A failed one is overwritten by\n    ///      the next cycle that reveals the spawn point, because a failed spawn\n    ///      point is free.\n    struct SpawnRecord {\n        uint64 cycle;\n        uint32 count;\n        bool blocked;\n        uint64 arrivedIn;\n        uint32 armyIndex;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The army registry.\n    mapping(uint256 army => ArmyRecord) internal _armies;\n    /// @notice Every army ever created, in order: what the registry pages over,\n    ///         and what turns an army's compact index back into its id\n    ///         ({_armyAt}).\n    uint256[] internal _armyIds;\n    /// @notice How many armies each account has created; its next is one more.\n    mapping(address owner => uint256 count) internal _armyCountOf;\n\n    /// @notice THE KINGS AND STONES EACH ARMY MAY HAVE TAKEN, for its stake.\n    /// @dev A SUPERSET, written at reveal time by the reveal that could make\n    ///      the capture (see `UsingGameBoard-_noteCandidate`), and filtered when\n    ///      read: an entry counts only if the stake of the army it names really\n    ///      went to this one (`UsingGameBoard-_captureOf`), which a stone's\n    ///      did not. The ORDER of the\n    ///      entries can differ with the order of the reveals, and an army can be\n    ///      listed more than once; what they add up to cannot differ.\n    mapping(uint256 army => uint256[] victims) internal _capturesBy;\n\n    /// @notice AN EXIT'S PAYOUT IN PROGRESS: the armies whose stakes the\n    ///         exited army took, down the tree of captures, still to collect, and what has been collected.\n    /// @dev See `UsingGameInternal-_collect`. Only ever written by an exit's\n    ///      own transactions, never by a reveal.\n    mapping(uint256 army => uint256[] armies) internal _toCollect;\n    mapping(uint256 army => uint256 amount) internal _collected;\n\n    /// @notice Deployments, by the spiral index of their spawn point.\n    mapping(uint256 index => SpawnRecord) internal _spawns;\n\n    /// @notice The per-square layer, by packed position.\n    mapping(uint64 position => SquareRecord) internal _squares;\n\n    /// @notice THE ZONE INDEX: for each 16x16 zone (`PositionUtils.getZone`),\n    ///         a bit per square that has a record, so the viewport read finds\n    ///         them without reading every square in view.\n    /// @dev Only ever OR-ed into, so the set it holds is the same whatever\n    ///      order the reveals land in, and so is the order the read lists it.\n    mapping(uint64 zone => uint256 squares) internal _touchedSquares;\n\n    /// @notice THE OPEN SET as it was last written: the spiral indices of the\n    ///         open spawn points, and the first index never yet open.\n    /// @dev Its invariant is what keeps reading it bounded: every index below\n    ///      `_nextSpawnIndex` that is not in `_openSpawnIndices` has had a\n    ///      deployment land on it, and nothing at or above `_nextSpawnIndex` has\n    ///      ever been open, so nothing there has ever been deployed to. So the\n    ///      open set at the start of any later cycle is this one with each\n    ///      entry that has since been deployed to replaced by the next fresh\n    ///      index: K reads, whatever has happened. Written by a deployment's\n    ///      reveal whenever that replacement changes it; empty (with\n    ///      `_nextSpawnIndex` zero) until the first, which reads as the first K\n    ///      indices.\n    uint64[] internal _openSpawnIndices;\n    uint64 internal _nextSpawnIndex;\n\n    /// @notice THE ARMIES A CYCLE THAT ADVANCES MAY BE WAITING FOR: every army\n    ///         created under the `Manual` or `TimedWithEarlyAdvance` policy\n    ///         that the advance has not yet found dead (`_sweepDeadArmies`).\n    /// @dev Empty under `Timed`, where nothing reads the waited-for count.\n    ///      Bounded by the seats a world or a table has, because only those\n    ///      policies fill it.\n    uint256[] internal _awaitedArmies;\n\n    /// @notice A TABLE'S OWN STATE: its spawn counter and its end.\n    /// @dev Untouched in the persistent world. See `UsingGameTable`.\n    struct TableState {\n        /// @notice how many spawn points its seats have been given: the next\n        ///         seat takes this spiral index. ONLY EVER INCREASES, so a\n        ///         seat that leaves leaves a gap and moves nobody else.\n        uint32 spawned;\n        /// @notice how many kings stood at the cap, for an even split when\n        ///         nobody has any material left\n        uint32 standing;\n        /// @notice whether the table's outcome and pot are written\n        bool settled;\n        /// @notice whether the material at the cap is counted\n        bool tallied;\n        /// @notice how far the count has got (see `UsingGameTable-_tally`)\n        uint64 tallyCursor;\n        /// @notice every stake on the table, once settled: what is paid out\n        uint256 pot;\n        /// @notice the material of every standing army at the cap, summed\n        uint256 totalMaterial;\n        /// @notice the last king standing, if the table ended that way\n        uint256 winner;\n    }\n    TableState internal _table;\n\n    /// @notice AT A TABLE, every zone a reveal has touched a square of, once\n    ///         each, in the order first touched: what the count of material\n    ///         at the cap walks (`UsingGameTable-_tally`), since the zone\n    ///         index alone cannot be listed.\n    /// @dev Written only when a zone's bits go from none to some, and only\n    ///      under a roster, so the world's reveals never pay for it.\n    uint64[] internal _tableZones;\n\n    /// @notice The material each standing army holds at a table's cap.\n    mapping(uint256 army => uint256 material) internal _materialOf;\n\n    /// @notice The id of the army with compact index `index`; zero for zero.\n    /// @dev `_armyIds[index - 1]` without the bounds check, which would read\n    ///      the array's length: an index is only ever written for an army that\n    ///      was pushed, and it is never removed.\n    function _armyAt(uint32 index) internal view returns (uint256 army) {\n        if (index == 0) return 0;\n        assembly (\"memory-safe\") {\n            mstore(0, _armyIds.slot)\n            army := sload(add(keccak256(0, 32), sub(index, 1)))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The compact index of `army`; zero for zero, or for an army that\n    ///         does not exist.\n    function _indexOf(uint256 army) internal view returns (uint32) {\n        if (army == 0) return 0;\n        return _armies[army].index;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Register a AGPL-3.0\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nimport \"../internal/UsingGameInternal.sol\";\nimport \"../interfaces/IGame.sol\";\n\n/// @dev THE ARMY REGISTRY, RESOLVED: every army, whether it stands and UsingGameInternal {\n    constructor(Config memory config) UsingGameInternal(config) {}\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGameRegistry\n    function getArmy(uint256 army) external view returns (ArmyView memory) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return _armyView(army, cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGameRegistry\n    function getArmies(\n        uint256 offset,\n        uint256 limit\n    ) external view returns (ArmyView[] memory armies, uint256 total) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        total = _armyIds.length;\n        uint256 end =\n            offset >= total\n                ? offset\n                : (limit > total - offset ? total : offset + limit);\n        armies = new ArmyView[](end - offset);\n        for (uint256 i = offset; i < end; i++) {\n            armies[i - offset] = _armyView(_armyIds[i], cycleNumber);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGameRegistry\n    function getArmiesOf(\n        address owner\n    ) external view returns (ArmyView[] memory armies) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        uint256 count = _armyCountOf[owner];\n        armies = new ArmyView[](count);\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n            armies[i] = _armyView(_armyIdOf(owner, i + 1), cycleNumber);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGameRegistry\n    function getNextArmy(address owner) external view returns (uint256 army) {\n        return _armyIdOf(owner, _armyCountOf[owner] + 1);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGameRegistry\n    function isFrozen(uint256 army) external view returns (bool) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return _isFrozen(army, cycleNumber);\n AGPL-3.0\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nlibrary PositionUtils {\n    function toXY(uint64 position) internal pure returns (int32 x, int32 y) {\n        x = int32(uint32(position) & 0xFFFFFFFF);\n        y = int32(uint32(position >> 32));\n    }\n\n    function fromXY(int32 x, int32 y) internal pure returns (uint64 position) {\n        position = (uint64(uint32(y)) << 32) + uint64(uint32(x));\n    }\n\n    function offset(\n        uint64 position,\n        int32 x,\n        int32 y\n    ) internal pure returns (uint64 newPosition) {\n        x = int32(uint32(position) & 0xFFFFFFFF) + x;\n        y = int32(uint32(position >> 32)) + y;\n        newPosition = (uint64(uint32(y)) << 32) + uint64(uint32(x));\n    }\n\n    int32 constant ZONE_SIZE = 16;\n    int32 constant ZONE_OFFSET = 8;\n\n    function zoneCoord(int32 a) internal pure returns (int32 b) {\n        if (a >= 0) {\n            b = (a + ZONE_OFFSET) / ZONE_SIZE;\n        } else {\n            // b = -((-a + ZONE_OFFSET) / ZONE_SIZE);\n            int256 absA = -a;\n            int256 negPart = (absA + ZONE_OFFSET - 1) / ZONE_SIZE; // ceil division\n            b = int32(-negPart);\n        }\n    }\n\n    function zoneCoords(\n        int32 x,\n        int32 y\n    ) internal pure returns (int32 zoneX, int32 zoneY) {\n        zoneX = zoneCoord(x);\n        zoneY = zoneCoord(y);\n    }\n\n    function getZone(uint64 position) internal pure returns (uint64 zone) {\n        (int32 x, int32 y) = toXY(position);\n        (int32 zoneX, int32 zoneY) = zoneCoords(x, y);\n        zone = (uint64(uint32(zoneY)) << 32) + uint64(uint32(zoneX));\n    }\n\n    function getZone(int32 x, int32 y) internal pure returns (uint64 zone) {\n        (int32 zoneX, int32 zoneY) = zoneCoords(x, y);\n        zone = (uint64(uint32(zoneY)) << 32) + uint64(uint32(zoneX));\n    }\n\n    function zoneLocalCoord(int32 x) internal pure returns (uint8 index) {\n        return uint8(uint32(x - (zoneCoord(x) * ZONE_SIZE - ZONE_OFFSET)));\n    }\n\n    function zoneLocalIndex(\n        int32 x,\n        int32 y\n    ) internal pure returns (uint8 index) {\n        uint8 zx = zoneLocalCoord(x);\n        uint8 zy = zoneLocalCoord(y);\n        return uint8(zy * uint32(ZONE_SIZE)) + zx;\n    }\n\n    function zoneLocalIndex(\n        uint64 position\n    ) internal pure returns (uint8 index) {\n        (int32 x, int32 y) = toXY(position);\n        return zoneLocalIndex(x, y);\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x6751af9d645f6a73fa0d7e20c85d0c36af57193072c8c0fc18dd0cc133abf6d2","license":"AGPL-3.0"}},"version":1}

AlreadyPaid(uint256).notice: The exited army's stake was already paid.

BondTooLow(uint256,uint256).notice: the revealed chunk costs more than the bond still set aside

CanStillReveal(uint64).notice: the player can still reveal, so the commitment cannot be voided

CommitmentHashNotMatching().notice: the revealed chunk does not hash to the head of the chain

CommitmentStillOpen(uint64).notice: cannot stop being a member while a turn of yours is still open

GameAlreadyStarted().notice: the game has started, so its roster is closed

GameEnded(uint64).notice: this game has played its last cycle: no commitment, advance or         forfeit any more

GameFull(uint8).notice: every seat of this game is taken

GameNotStarted().notice: the game has not started yet

IllegalMove(uint64,uint64).notice: The move is not one this army may make on the board as it stood         at the start of the cycle.

InCommitmentPhase(uint64).notice: trying to reveal while the commit phase is running

InRevealPhase(uint64).notice: trying to commit while the reveal phase is running

InvalidActionsPerReveal().notice: a chunk size of zero, which would make every turn unrevealable

InvalidCreator().notice: a roster needs a creator, who is the only one who can start it

InvalidCycle(uint64,uint64).notice: the commitment belongs to a different cycle

InvalidCycleConfiguration().notice: the phase durations do not describe a cycle this game can run

InvalidCycles(uint16).notice: a game for a fixed set of members plays at least one cycle

InvalidDeployment().notice: A deployment's reveal must hold exactly one `Move` whose `from`         and `to` are both the spawn point, in one chunk.

InvalidFurtherActions(uint256,uint256).notice: a reveal that promises more actions did not carry a full chunk

InvalidPlayer(uint256).notice: this identity cannot play this game

InvalidSeats(uint8).notice: a roster must hold at least two members

InvalidSpawnGrid().notice: The deployment parameters cannot make a board: spawn points         closer than an army's footprint, or no spawn point ever open.

MemberHasActed(uint256,uint64).notice: this member has acted in the current phase, so the creator         cannot forfeit them

NextPhaseNotAllowed().notice: this game's cycle is advanced by the clock and by nothing else

NoCommitmentToCancel().notice: there is no commitment to cancel

NoOneToWaitFor().notice: nobody is being waited for, so unanimity has no denominator

NoRoster().notice: this game has open entry, so it has no roster to act on

NotASpawnPoint(uint64).notice: The position is not on the spawn grid.

NotArmyOwner(uint256).notice: Only the account that owns an army may take its stake back.

NotEnoughMembers(uint256).notice: a game starts with at least two members seated

NotExited(uint256).notice: The army has not left the board through an exit (yet).

NotInGame(uint256).notice: this identity has not entered the game, so it cannot take a turn

NothingToClaim(uint256).notice: The army is owed nothing by the table's outcome.

NothingToReveal().notice: there is no commitment to reveal or to void

OneMovePerCycle().notice: A submission after an army's deployment is ONE move, in one         chunk: a pass (nothing) or up to three piece-moves, each by a         different piece and none two to one square (`docs/adr/0016`).

PreviousCommitmentNotRevealed().notice: an earlier commitment was never revealed; resolve it first

ReserveTooLow(uint256,uint256).notice: the player's reserve cannot cover this

RosterAlreadyOpened().notice: this game's roster was already opened

SpawnPointNotOpen(uint64).notice: The spawn point was not open at the start of this cycle.

StillWaitingToCommit(uint64,uint64).notice: some of the members the cycle waits for have not committed yet

StillWaitingToReveal(uint64,uint64).notice: some of this cycle's commitments have not been revealed yet

TableNotOver().notice: Neither one king stands nor is the table's last cycle over.

TooManyActions(uint256,uint256).notice: this reveal carries more actions than one transaction may

UnreadableGameOptions(bytes32).notice: The table was created with `gameOptions` this game cannot read         (a bit set other than `ChessRules.ONE_PIECE_MOVE`), so nobody         may take a seat at it.

WrongStake(uint256,uint256).notice: A table's seat is bought with exactly one stake.

ArmyCreated(uint256,address,uint64,uint2.notice: A deployment was committed, which created the army and moved the         stake from its owner's reserve into its own.

ArmyFrozen(uint256).notice: An army's missed reveal of a move was settled, which froze it         for good. It was frozen already from the close of that reveal         window (`IGameRegistry-isFrozen`); this is only the settling.

CommitmentCancelled(uint256,uint64).notice: A player withdrew their commitment before the reveal phase.

CommitmentMade(uint256,uint64,bytes24,ui.notice: A player committed to a turn for this cycle.

CommitmentRevealed(uint256,uint64,bytes2.notice: A player revealed a chunk of what they had committed to.

CommitmentVoid(uint256,uint64,bytes24,by.notice: A missed reveal was settled, in whole or by one chunk.

CycleAdvanced(uint64,bool,address).notice: The cycle moved because somebody pushed it, rather than because         the clock said so.

DeploymentRefunded(uint256,address,uint2.notice: A deployment that failed (a shared spawn point, a blocked         footprint) or was cancelled had its stake moved back from the         army's reserve to its owner's account reserve.

DeploymentRevealed(uint256,uint64,uint64.notice: A deployment was revealed. Whether it lands is decided when the         cycle is over, by how many deployments revealed the same spawn         point, so this says nothing about the outcome.

ExitPaid(uint256,address,uint256).notice: An exited army's whole stake was paid, in ETH, to its owner.

GameStarted(address,uint256,uint64).notice: The creator started the game, which closes its roster.

MemberForfeited(uint256,uint64).notice: The creator forfeited a member who had not acted in the         current phase: the cycle stops waiting for them, for good.

ReserveDeposited(uint256,uint256,uint256.notice: A player topped up the reserve they are willing to risk.

ReserveWithdrawn(uint256,uint256,uint256.notice: A player took tokens back out of their reserve.

RosterOpened(address,uint8,uint16,bytes3.notice: A closed roster was opened: the game now has `seats` seats, a         creator who starts it, and plays `cycles` cycles from its start.

SeatReleased(uint256,uint256).notice: A member left their seat: by emptying their reserve, or by         being forfeited.

SeatTaken(uint256,uint256).notice: A member took a seat, by funding a reserve.

StakeBurned(uint256,uint256).notice: A deployment that was never revealed had its stake burned.

TableLeft(uint256,address,uint256).notice: A table's army left before it started, its stake returned.

TableSeatTaken(uint256,uint64).notice: A table's army took spawn point `spawnPoint`, bought in.

TableSettled(uint256,uint256,uint256).notice: A table's outcome is written: its winner (zero for a split by         material) and every stake on it.

WaitedForChanged(uint256,bool,uint64).notice: The cycle started, or stopped, waiting for this player.

getArmies(uint256,uint256).notice: THE ARMY REGISTRY, a page at a time, resolved: every army ever         created, in the order they were.

isFrozen(uint256).notice: Whether `army` is FROZEN by a missed reveal: it never moves         again and its king cannot exit, but it can still be captured         (`docs/adr/0005-missed-reveal-freezes-the-army.md`).
